units.zh: 溫嶠
units.en: Wen Jiao.
units.literal: Wen Jiao.

units.zh: 溫嶠，字太真，司徒羨弟之子也。
units.en: Wen Jiao, courtesy name Taizhen, was the son of Wen Dan, younger brother of Minister of Education Wen Xian.
units.literal: Wen Jiao, courtesy name Taizhen, was the son of Wen Dan, younger brother of Minister of Education Xian.

units.zh: 父憺，河東太守。
units.en: His father, Wen Dan, served as administrator of Hedong commandery.
units.literal: His father Dan was Administrator of Hedong.

units.zh: 嶠性聰敏，有識量，博學能屬文，少以孝悌稱於邦族。
units.en: Wen Jiao was quick-witted and discerning, erudite and a capable writer; even as a youth he was known among his kinsmen for filial devotion and fraternal respect.
units.literal: Jiao was clever and keen by nature, had judgment and breadth of mind, was broadly learned and could compose texts; in youth he was praised among his clan for filial piety and brotherly duty.

units.zh: 風儀秀整，美於談論，見者皆愛悅之。
units.en: He carried himself with polished grace and spoke with uncommon eloquence; everyone who met him warmed to him at once.
units.literal: His bearing was refined and composed; he excelled in conversation; those who met him all loved and delighted in him.

units.zh: 年十七，州郡辟召，皆不就。
units.en: When he was seventeen, local authorities repeatedly offered him posts; he declined them all.
units.literal: At age seventeen, provincial and commandery authorities summoned him to office; he accepted none.

units.zh: 司隸命為都官從事。
units.en: The Metropolitan Governor then appointed him assistant for capital affairs.
units.literal: The Metropolitan Governor appointed him Assistant for Capital Officials.

units.zh: 散騎常侍庾敳有重名，而頗聚斂，嶠舉奏之，京都振肅。
units.en: Yu Ai, the attendant cavalry regular, enjoyed wide renown but also enriched himself through graft; Wen Jiao memorialized against him, and order tightened across the capital.
units.literal: Attendant Cavalry Regular Yu Ai had a great reputation but gathered wealth through exactions; Jiao impeached him in a memorial, and the capital was shaken into discipline.

units.zh: 後舉秀才、灼然。
units.en: He was later nominated as a cultivated talent and passed the Zhuoran examination.
units.literal: Later he was recommended as Cultivated Talent and as Zhuoran.

units.zh: 司徒辟東閣祭酒，補上黨潞令。
units.en: The Minister of Education appointed him libationer of the Eastern Pavilion, after which he served as magistrate of Lu county in Shangdang.
units.literal: The Minister of Education summoned him as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion; he was appointed Magistrate of Lu in Shangdang.

units.zh: 平北大將軍劉琨妻，嶠之從母也。
units.en: The wife of Liu Kun—general bearing the title Pacifier of the North—was Wen Jiao's aunt on his mother's side.
units.literal: The wife of General Who Pacifies the North Liu Kun was Jiao's maternal aunt.

units.zh: 琨深禮之，請為參軍。
units.en: Liu Kun received him with exceptional respect and invited him to serve as military adviser.
units.literal: Kun treated him with great courtesy and requested him as military adviser.

units.zh: 琨遷大將軍，嶠為從事中郎、上黨太守，加建威將軍、督護前鋒軍事。
units.en: When Liu Kun rose to Grand General, Wen Jiao followed as senior clerk and administrator of Shangdang, with the added ranks of General Who Establishes Might and supervisor of the vanguard forces.
units.literal: When Kun was promoted to Grand General, Jiao became senior clerk, Administrator of Shangdang, with additional titles General Who Establishes Might and supervisor who protects the vanguard army.

units.zh: 將兵討石勒，屢有戰功。
units.en: He campaigned against Shi Le and won repeated distinction on the battlefield.
units.literal: He led troops against Shi Le and repeatedly achieved merit in battle.

units.zh: 琨遷司空，以嶠為右司馬。
units.en: When Liu Kun advanced to Minister of Works, he named Wen Jiao chief of staff on the right.
units.literal: When Kun was promoted to Minister of Works, he appointed Jiao as Right Army Supervisor.

units.zh: 于時并土荒殘，寇盜群起，石勒、劉聰跨帶疆場，嶠為之謀主，琨所憑恃焉。
units.en: Bingzhou lay in ruins, rebels sprang up everywhere, and Shi Le and Liu Cong dominated the borderlands; Wen Jiao became Liu Kun's chief strategist—the man on whom he depended.
units.literal: At that time Bing province was desolate and ruined; bandits rose in swarms; Shi Le and Liu Cong straddled the frontiers; Jiao was the chief planner for this, on whom Kun relied.

units.zh: 屬二都傾覆，社稷絕祀，元帝初鎮江左，琨誠繫王室，謂嶠曰：「昔班彪識劉氏之復興，馬援知漢光之可輔。
units.en: After Luoyang and Chang'an fell and the dynasty's altars went cold, while the Prince of Langye was still consolidating his position south of the Yangzi, Liu Kun—whose heart was fixed on the house of Jin—said to Wen Jiao: "Long ago Ban Biao saw the Liu clan's restoration coming; Ma Yuan knew Liu Xiu was worth serving.
units.literal: When both capitals had fallen and sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain ceased, and the Yuan Emperor first established himself south of the Yangzi, Kun was sincerely attached to the royal house and said to Jiao: "In old days Ban Biao recognized the Liu family's revival; Ma Yuan knew that Guangwu of Han could be aided.

units.zh: 今晉祚雖衰，天命未改，吾欲立功河朔，使卿延譽江南，子其行乎？」
units.en: The mandate of Jin may be fraying, but Heaven has not yet changed its charge. I intend to win merit on the northern plain while you carry our cause to the south—will you go?"
units.literal: Now the Jin mandate though declining, Heaven's appointment has not changed; I wish to establish merit north of the river and send you to extend your reputation south of the Yangzi—will you go?

units.zh: 對曰：「嶠雖無管張之才，而明公有桓文之志，欲建匡合之功，豈敢辭命。」
units.en: Wen Jiao answered, "I am no Guan Zhong or Zhang Liang, yet you, my lord, harbor the ambitions of a Duke Huan or Duke Wen. If I may help restore order to the realm, I would not dream of refusing."
units.literal: He replied: "Though Jiao lacks the talents of Guan [Zhong] and Zhang [Liang], my enlightened lord has the aspirations of Huan [of Qi] and Wen [of Jin]; desiring to establish the merit of restoring order to the realm, how dare I decline the charge?"

units.zh: 乃以為左長史，檄告華夷，奉表勸進。
units.en: Liu Kun thereupon appointed him senior clerk on the left, issued proclamations to Chinese and non-Chinese alike, and submitted a memorial urging the prince to assume the throne.
units.literal: Thereupon he was made senior clerk on the left, proclaimed by edict to Chinese and barbarians, and presented a memorial urging advance to the throne.

units.zh: 嶠既至，引見，具陳琨忠誠，志在效節，因說社稷無主，天人係望，辭旨慷慨。
units.en: Once Wen Jiao reached the court, he was received in audience. He laid out Liu Kun's loyalty and steadfast resolve, then explained that the altars stood without a rightful lord and that both Heaven and the people looked to a leader—speaking with fierce conviction.
units.literal: When Jiao arrived, he was granted audience and fully set forth Kun's loyalty and resolve to devote himself; he then spoke of how the altars had no master and Heaven and men hung their hopes, his words stirring and impassioned.

units.zh: 舉朝屬目，帝器而嘉焉。
units.en: The entire court watched him with expectation; the emperor valued him highly and praised him openly.
units.literal: The whole court fixed its eyes on him; the emperor esteemed and praised him.

units.zh: 王導、周顗、謝鯤、庾亮、桓彝等並與親善。
units.en: He formed close ties with Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Xie Kun, Yu Liang, Huan Yi, and others.
units.literal: Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Xie Kun, Yu Liang, Huan Yi, and others all became intimate and friendly with him.

units.zh: 于時江左草創，綱維未舉，嶠殊以為憂。
units.en: The southern court was still taking shape and its institutions were hardly in place; Wen Jiao found this deeply troubling.
units.literal: At that time the land south of the Yangzi was newly founded and its institutions not yet established; Jiao was greatly troubled by this.

units.zh: 及見王導共談，歡然曰；
units.en: After meeting Wang Dao and speaking with him at length, he exclaimed with relief,
units.literal: When he saw Wang Dao and conversed with him together, he happily said;

units.zh: 「江左自有管夷吾，吾復何慮！」
units.en: "The south has its own Guan Zhong—I have nothing left to fear!"
units.literal: "South of the Yangzi there is already Guan Yiwu—what more need I worry!"

units.zh: 屢求反命，不許。
units.en: He repeatedly asked leave to return north with his answer; each time the court refused.
units.literal: He repeatedly requested permission to return with his report; it was not granted.

units.zh: 會琨為段匹磾所害，嶠表琨忠誠，雖勳業不遂，然家破身亡，宜在褒崇，以慰海內之望。
units.en: When Duan Pidi murdered Liu Kun, Wen Jiao memorialized on Liu Kun's loyalty: his great enterprise had gone unfinished, yet he had sacrificed family and life alike; the throne should honor him to satisfy sentiment across the realm.
units.literal: When Kun was killed by Duan Pidi, Jiao submitted a memorial on Kun's loyalty: though his merit was not completed, yet his family was broken and he himself perished; he ought to be honored and exalted to console expectations within the seas.

units.zh: 帝然之。
units.en: The emperor agreed.
units.literal: The emperor approved it.

units.zh: 除散騎侍郎。
units.en: He was appointed attendant gentleman at the palace gates.
units.literal: He was appointed Gentleman Attendant at Yellow Gates.

units.zh: 初，嶠欲將命，其母崔氏固止之，嶠絕裾而去。
units.en: When Wen Jiao first prepared to answer Liu Kun's summons, his mother Lady Cui tried to stop him; he tore the hem from her grasp and left anyway.
units.literal: At first, when Jiao wished to carry out his mission, his mother Lady Cui firmly stopped him; Jiao tore off the hem of his robe and departed.

units.zh: 其後母亡，嶠阻亂不獲歸葬，由是固讓不拜，苦請北歸。
units.en: After she died, chaos along the route kept him from returning her remains for burial; he therefore repeatedly declined office and pleaded to be allowed north.
units.literal: Later his mother died; Jiao was blocked by turmoil and could not return to bury her; therefore he firmly declined appointment and did not take office, bitterly requesting to return north.

units.zh: 詔三司、八坐議其事，皆曰：「昔伍員志復私讎，先假諸侯之力，東奔闔閭，位為上將，然後鞭荊王之尸。
units.en: The throne ordered the chief ministers to debate the matter. Their verdict: "Long ago Wu Zixu sought private vengeance; he borrowed strength from the feudal lords, fled east to King Helü of Wu, rose to chief commander, and only then lashed the corpse of the king of Chu.
units.literal: An edict ordered the Three Offices and the Eight Seats to deliberate; they all said: "In old days Wu Yuan aimed to avenge a private grudge; first borrowing the power of the feudal lords, he fled east to Helü and rose to chief general, then whipped the corpse of the king of Jing.

units.zh: 若嶠以母未葬沒在胡虜者，乃應竭其智謀，仰憑皇靈，使逆寇冰消，反哀墓次，豈可稍以乖嫌，廢其遠圖哉！」
units.en: If Wen Jiao must leave his mother's bones in barbarian hands until he can redeem them, he should bend every stratagem to crush the rebels under Heaven's blessing—then return to weep at her grave. Shall we discard so vital a design over personal resentment?"
units.literal: If Jiao, because his mother is unburied and lost among the Hu captives, ought then to exhaust his schemes and rely on the imperial numen to make the rebellious bandits melt like ice and return to mourn at her tomb—how can we for slight alienation abandon his long-range plans!

units.zh: 嶠不得已，乃受命。
units.en: Wen Jiao had no choice but to accept the post.
units.literal: Jiao had no choice and then accepted the appointment.

units.zh: 後歷驃騎王導長史，遷太子中庶子。
units.en: He later served as chief administrator under Wang Dao, general of agile cavalry, then rose to senior adviser in the heir apparent's household.
units.literal: Later he successively served as senior clerk to Wang Dao, General of Agile Cavalry, and was promoted to Palace Minister to the heir apparent.

units.zh: 及在東宮，深見寵遇，太子與為布衣之交。
units.en: At the heir's residence he enjoyed exceptional favor; the crown prince treated him as an intimate friend.
units.literal: When he was in the Eastern Palace, he was deeply favored; the heir apparent had with him the friendship of common cloth.

units.zh: 數陳規諷，又獻《侍臣箴》，甚有弘益。
units.en: He offered frequent counsel and presented his "Admonition for Palace Attendants," to great practical benefit.
units.literal: He repeatedly presented admonitions and remonstrance, and also presented the "Admonition for Attendant Ministers," which was greatly beneficial.

units.zh: 時太子起西池樓觀，頗為勞費，嶠上疏以為朝廷草創，巨寇未滅，宜應儉以率下，務農重兵，太子納焉。
units.en: The crown prince had raised elaborate towers and pavilions beside the West Pool at considerable cost; Wen Jiao argued in a memorial that the court was still new and major enemies remained—the ruler should model austerity, stress farming, and build military strength. The heir took his advice.
units.literal: At the time the heir apparent built towers and belvederes at the West Pond, quite laborious and costly; Jiao submitted a memorial holding that the court was newly founded and great bandits not yet destroyed; one ought to be frugal to lead those below, prioritize agriculture and emphasize military affairs; the heir apparent accepted it.

units.zh: 王敦舉兵內向，六軍敗績，太子將自出戰，嶠執鞚諫曰：「臣聞善戰者不怒，善勝者不武，如何萬乘儲副而以身輕天下！」
units.en: When Wang Dun marched on the capital and the imperial armies collapsed, the crown prince meant to ride out himself; Wen Jiao seized the reins and warned, "The sage commander masters anger before battle; true victory needs no bluster. How can the heir to the throne stake the empire on a single sortie?"
units.literal: When Wang Dun raised troops inward, the six armies were routed; the heir apparent was about to go out to battle himself; Jiao seized the reins and remonstrated: "Your subject has heard that those good at war are not angry, those good at victory do not rely on force—how can the heir of ten thousand chariots lightly hazard himself before the realm!"

units.zh: 太子乃止。
units.en: The prince relented.
units.literal: The heir apparent then stopped.

units.zh: 明帝即位，拜侍中，機密大謀皆所參綜，詔命文翰亦悉豫焉。
units.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Wen Jiao became palace attendant: he helped shape every confidential decision and joined in drafting the emperor's edicts and correspondence.
units.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, he was appointed palace attendant; secret great plans were all coordinated by him; edicts and documents he also fully participated in.

units.zh: 俄轉中書令。
units.en: He soon advanced to director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 嶠有棟梁之任，帝親而倚之，甚為王敦所忌，因請為左司馬。
units.en: Wen Jiao carried the weight of a chief minister; the emperor trusted him utterly—so Wang Dun, who resented that influence, secured his appointment as Dun's chief of staff on the left.
units.literal: Jiao had the responsibility of a pillar and ridge-beam; the emperor was intimate with and relied on him; Wang Dun greatly envied him and therefore requested him as Left Army Supervisor.

units.zh: 敦阻兵不朝，多行陵縱，嶠諫敦曰：「昔周公之相成王，勞謙吐握，豈好勤而惡逸哉！
units.en: Wang Dun kept his army idle and stayed away from court, behaving with brutal arrogance; Wen Jiao remonstrated: "Long ago the Duke of Zhou served the young king with exhausting humility—spitting out food and wringing his wet hair—not because he enjoyed drudgery or despised rest!
units.literal: Dun blocked troops and did not attend court, often behaving arrogantly and licentiously; Jiao remonstrated with Dun: "In old days the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, toiling modestly, spitting out food and loosening hair—was it because he loved toil and hated ease!

units.zh: 誠由處大任者不可不爾。
units.en: No—great responsibility leaves no room for ease.
units.literal: Truly because one who bears great responsibility must be thus.

units.zh: 而公自還輦轂，入輔朝政，闕拜覲之禮，簡人臣之儀，不達聖心者莫不於邑。
units.en: Yet you now reside at the capital as chief minister without attending court, skipping audiences and flouting the deportment owed a subject—every loyal official grieves at it.
units.literal: Yet since my lord returned to the capital region and entered to assist court governance, you omit the rites of audience and simplify the ceremonies of a subject—those who do not comprehend the sagely mind none fail to grieve.

units.zh: 昔帝舜服事唐堯，伯禹竭身虞庭，文王雖盛，臣節不諐。
units.en: Emperor Shun served Yao with humility; Yu gave himself wholly to Shun's court; even mighty King Wen never slipped from proper subservience.
units.literal: In old days Emperor Shun served Tang Yao; Bo Yu exhausted himself in the court of Yu; King Wen though flourishing did not fault in ministerial integrity.

units.zh: 故有庇人之大德，必有事君之小心，俾芳烈奮乎百世，休風流乎萬祀。
units.en: Those who shelter the people also honor their sovereign with painstaking loyalty—that is how their fame lasts centuries and their example endures forever.
units.literal: Therefore where there is great virtue that shelters others, there must be careful mind in serving the ruler, causing fragrant merit to blaze through a hundred generations and elegant influence to flow through ten thousand sacrifices.

units.zh: 至聖遺軌，所不宜忽。
units.en: The example of the greatest sages must never be cast aside.
units.literal: The tracks left by the utmost sage ought not be neglected.

units.zh: 願思舜、禹、文王服事之勤，惟公旦吐握之事，則天下幸甚。」
units.en: Remember how Shun, Yu, and King Wen served their lords, and how the Duke of Zhou broke off every meal to receive visitors—the empire would be profoundly blessed."
units.literal: I wish you to ponder the diligence of Shun, Yu, and King Wen in service, and the spitting food and loosening hair of the Duke of Zhou—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.

units.zh: 敦不納。
units.en: Wang Dun brushed the advice aside.
units.literal: Dun did not accept it.

units.zh: 嶠知其終不悟，於是謬為設敬，綜其府事，干說密謀，以附其欲。
units.en: Seeing that Wang Dun would never relent, Wen Jiao feigned deference, ran headquarters business, and fed him stratagems that matched Dun's ambitions.
units.literal: Jiao knew he would never come to understanding; then falsely showed respect, managed his headquarters affairs, intervened with secret schemes to attach to his desires.

units.zh: 深結錢鳳，為之聲譽，每曰：「錢世儀精神滿腹。」
units.en: He cultivated Qian Feng assiduously, praising him at every turn—"Qian Shiyi has wit enough to fill his belly."
units.literal: He deeply befriended Qian Feng, building reputation for him, often saying: "Qian Shiyi is full of spirit and intellect in his belly.

units.zh: 嶠素有知人之稱，鳳聞而悅之，深結好於嶠。
units.en: Wen Jiao's judgment of character was legendary; Qian Feng, pleased by the praise, drew close to him.
units.literal: Jiao always had a reputation for knowing men; Feng heard and was pleased, deeply befriending Jiao.

units.zh: 會丹陽尹缺，嶠說敦曰：「京尹輦轂喉舌，宜得文武兼能，公宜自選其才。
units.en: When the governorship of Danyang fell vacant, Wen Jiao urged Wang Dun: "The capital intendant speaks for the throne; you need someone versed in both civil and military affairs—choose the man yourself.
units.literal: When the office of Governor of Danyang was vacant, Jiao persuaded Dun: "The capital governor is the throat and tongue of the imperial carriage region; one ought to obtain someone both civil and martial capable; my lord ought yourself to select the talent.

units.zh: 若朝廷用人，或不盡理。」
units.en: If you leave it to court factions, you may not get the right officer."
units.literal: If the court employs men, perhaps not entirely reasonably.

units.zh: 敦然之，問嶠誰可作者。
units.en: Wang Dun agreed and asked whom he should appoint.
units.literal: Dun approved and asked Jiao who could do it.

units.zh: 嶠曰：「愚謂錢鳳可用。」
units.en: Wen Jiao replied, "Qian Feng would serve admirably."
units.literal: Jiao said: "In my foolish opinion Qian Feng may be used.

units.zh: 鳳亦推嶠，嶠偽辭之。
units.en: Qian Feng in turn recommended Wen Jiao, who protested modestly.
units.literal: Feng also recommended Jiao; Jiao falsely declined.

units.zh: 敦不從，表補丹陽尹。
units.en: Wang Dun would hear none of it and memorialized Wen Jiao himself as governor of Danyang.
units.literal: Dun did not follow this and memorialized to appoint [Jiao] as Governor of Danyang.

units.zh: 嶠猶懼錢鳳為之姦謀，因敦餞別，嶠起行酒，至鳳前，鳳未及飲，嶠因偽醉，以手版擊鳳幘墜，作色曰：「錢鳳何人，溫太真行酒而敢不飲！」
units.en: Wen Jiao still feared Qian Feng's intrigues. At Wang Dun's farewell banquet he circulated the wine; when he reached Qian Feng, Feng had not yet lifted his cup. Wen Jiao feigned drunken rage, knocked Feng's headcloth off with his tablet, and shouted, "Who is Qian Feng that he refuses a cup from Wen Taizhen!"
units.literal: Jiao still feared Qian Feng would plot against him; at Dun's farewell feast, Jiao rose to pass wine; when he came before Feng, Feng had not yet drunk; Jiao then pretended drunkenness, struck Feng's cap off with his tablet, changed color and said: "What sort of person is Qian Feng—when Wen Taizhen passes wine he dares not drink!

units.zh: 敦以為醉，兩釋之。
units.en: Wang Dun dismissed it as a drunken spat and excused them both.
units.literal: Dun thought it drunkenness and released both.

units.zh: 臨去言別，涕泗橫流，出閤復入，如是再三，然後即路。
units.en: When he finally departed he wept openly, stepping out of the hall and back in again before he could bring himself to leave.
units.literal: When about to leave he bid farewell, tears and mucus flowing across; he went out of the chamber and re-entered, thus several times, then took the road.

units.zh: 及發後，鳳入說敦曰：「嶠於朝廷甚密，而與庾亮深交，未必可信。」
units.en: Once Wen Jiao had gone, Qian Feng warned Wang Dun, "He is thick with the court and intimate with Yu Liang—hardly reliable."
units.literal: After he had set out, Feng entered and spoke to Dun: "Jiao is very close to the court and deeply friendly with Yu Liang—not necessarily trustworthy.

units.zh: 敦曰：「太真昨醉，小加聲色，豈得以此便相讒貳。」
units.en: Wang Dun replied, "Taizhen was drunk last night; I merely scolded him—you cannot call that disloyalty."
units.literal: Dun said: "Taizhen yesterday was drunk; I slightly added harsh sound and color—how can we for this then slanderously doubt each other.

units.zh: 由是鳳謀不行，而嶠得還都，乃具奏敦之逆謀，請先為之備。
units.en: The warning went nowhere, and Wen Jiao reached the capital, where he laid out Wang Dun's conspiracy and urged immediate precautions.
units.literal: Therefore Feng's plot did not proceed, and Jiao was able to return to the capital, then fully memorialized Dun's rebellious plot and requested first to prepare against it.

units.zh: 及敦構逆，加嶠中壘將軍、持節、都督東安北部諸軍事。
units.en: When Wang Dun rose in revolt, Wen Jiao received the titles general of the central rampart, credential bearer, and area commander for the northern sector east of the capital.
units.literal: When Dun plotted rebellion, Jiao was additionally appointed General of the Central Rampart, Bearer of the Credential, and Area Commander of military affairs north of Dong'an.

units.zh: 敦與王導書曰：「太真別來幾日，作如此事！」
units.en: Wang Dun wrote to Wang Dao, "Taizhen has been gone only days—how dare he turn on me like this!"
units.literal: Dun wrote to Wang Dao: "Taizhen—how many days since we parted—and he does such things!

units.zh: 表誅姦臣，以嶠為首。
units.en: He memorialized for the execution of "treacherous ministers," naming Wen Jiao first.
units.literal: He memorialized to execute wicked ministers, with Jiao as chief.

units.zh: 募生得嶠者，當自拔其舌。
units.en: He promised reward to anyone who took Wen Jiao alive—then rip out his tongue.
units.literal: He offered a reward: whoever captures Jiao alive shall himself pull out his tongue.

units.zh: 及王含、錢鳳奄至都下，嶠燒朱雀桁以挫其鋒，帝怒之，嶠曰：「今宿衛寡弱，徵兵未至，若賊豕突，危及社稷，陛下何惜一橋。」
units.en: When Wang Han and Qian Feng suddenly appeared below the walls, Wen Jiao burned the Vermilion Sparrow Bridge to check their advance; the emperor rebuked him. Wen Jiao replied, "The palace guard is thin and reinforcements have not arrived—if the rebels break through like wild boars and threaten the altars, why cherish a wooden bridge?"
units.literal: When Wang Han and Qian Feng suddenly arrived below the capital, Jiao burned the Vermilion Bird Bridge to blunt their edge; the emperor was angry at him; Jiao said: "Now the night guards are few and weak, summoned troops have not arrived; if the bandits burst like boars, endangering altars and grain—why should Your Majesty spare one bridge!

units.zh: 賊果不得渡。
units.en: The rebels never forced the crossing.
units.literal: The bandits indeed could not cross.

units.zh: 嶠自率眾與賊夾水戰，擊王含，敗之，復督劉遐追錢鳳於江寧。
units.en: Wen Jiao led his troops in battle across the river, routed Wang Han, then directed Liu Xia's pursuit of Qian Feng at Jiangning.
units.literal: Jiao personally led the multitude and fought the bandits across the water, struck Wang Han and defeated him; again supervised Liu Xia pursuing Qian Feng at Jiangning.

units.zh: 事平，封建寧縣開國公，賜絹五千四百匹，進號前將軍。
units.en: After the victory he was enfeoffed as duke of Jianning with five thousand four hundred bolts of silk and promoted to general of the van.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Founded the Nation of Jianning county, granted five thousand four hundred bolts of silk, advanced in title to General of the Front.

units.zh: 時制王敦綱紀除名，參佐禁固，嶠上疏曰：「王敦剛愎不仁，忍行殺戮，親任小人，疎遠君子，朝廷所不能抑，骨肉所不能間。
units.en: Policy called for striking Wang Dun's staff from the rolls and detaining his aides. Wen Jiao memorialized: "Wang Dun was obstinate and merciless, slaughtered at will, favored petty men and spurned gentlemen—beyond the court's control and impervious even to kin.
units.literal: At the time the regulation was that Wang Dun's clerks were struck from registers and aides imprisoned; Jiao submitted a memorial: "Wang Dun was stubborn and cruel without benevolence, cruelly carried out killings, intimately employed petty men and estranged gentlemen—what the court could not restrain, what flesh and bone could not divide.

units.zh: 處其朝者恒懼危亡，故人士結舌，道路以目，誠賢人君子道窮數盡，遵養時晦之辰也。
units.en: Those who attended him lived in daily dread, so men fell silent and exchanged only glances in the street—it was the hour when good officials could only withdraw and bide their time.
units.literal: Those who served in his court constantly feared peril and death; therefore gentlemen sealed their tongues; on the roads they used eyes only—truly the time when worthy men and gentlemen' way was exhausted and fate ended, the season of nurturing and awaiting darkness.

units.zh: 且敦為大逆之日，拘錄人士，自免無路，原其私心，豈遑晏處，如陸玩、羊曼、劉胤、蔡謨、郭璞常與臣言，備知之矣。
units.en: Moreover, when Dun rebelled he seized hostages from among the gentry; none could escape. Lu Wan, Yang Man, Liu Yin, Cai Mo, and Guo Pu often confided in me—I know their hearts.
units.literal: Moreover when Dun committed great treason, he detained gentlemen; there was no road to save oneself; tracing their private hearts, how could they leisurely dwell—as Lu Wan, Yang Man, Liu Yin, Cai Mo, and Guo Pu often spoke with your subject, I fully know it.

units.zh: 必其凶悖，自可罪人斯得；
units.en: Where men were truly vicious, let justice take its course;
units.literal: If they were indeed fierce and perverse, naturally one may obtain the guilty;

units.zh: 如其枉入姦黨，宜施之以寬。
units.en: where they were swept into the net innocently, show mercy.
units.literal: if they were wrongly entered among the traitorous faction, one ought to apply leniency to them.

units.zh: 加以玩等之誠，聞於聖聽，當受同賊之責，實負其心。
units.en: Lu Wan and his fellows have proved their loyalty to Your Majesty's ears; to punish them as traitors would betray every honest impulse.
units.literal: Moreover Wan and others' sincerity has reached sagely hearing; they ought to bear the responsibility same as bandits—this truly betrays their hearts.

units.zh: 陛下仁聖含弘，思求允中；
units.en: You are humane and magnanimous; you seek a fair middle course;
units.literal: Your Majesty benevolent and sage, encompassing and magnanimous, thinking to seek what is balanced and right;

units.zh: 臣階緣博納，干非其事，誠在愛才，不忘忠益。」
units.en: I speak beyond my station only because I cherish worthy men and loyal counsel."
units.literal: your subject steps by broad acceptance, ventures beyond his affair—truly in loving talent, not forgetting loyal benefit.

units.zh: 帝從之。
units.en: The emperor granted his request.
units.literal: The emperor followed it.

units.zh: 是時天下凋弊，國用不足，詔公卿以下詣都坐論時政之所先，嶠因奏軍國要務。
units.en: The empire was impoverished and the treasury empty; the throne summoned senior officials to debate priorities, and Wen Jiao submitted his program for army and state.
units.literal: At this time the realm was withered and exhausted, state funds insufficient; an edict ordered dukes and ministers down to attend the capital seat to discuss what was prior in current governance; Jiao then memorialized military and state essentials.

units.zh: 其一曰：「祖約退舍壽陽，有將來之難。
units.en: First: "Zu Yue has pulled back toward Shouyang—trouble will follow.
units.literal: The first said: "Zu Yue withdrew his camp from Shouyang—there is difficulty coming.

units.zh: 今二方守禦，為功尚易。
units.en: For now both fronts can still be held without extreme effort.
units.literal: Now two sides defend—success is still easy.

units.zh: 淮泗都督，宜竭力以資之。
units.en: The commander on the Huai and Si must pour every resource into supporting them.
units.literal: The Huai-Si area commander ought to exhaust strength to aid them.

units.zh: 選名重之士，配征兵五千人，又擇一偏將，將二千兵，以益壽陽，可以保固徐豫，援助司土。」
units.en: Send a respected officer with five thousand levied troops and a deputy with another two thousand to thicken the line at Shouyang—that will secure Xu and Yu and relieve the central plain."
units.literal: Select a man of heavy reputation, assign conscripted troops five thousand men; also choose one deputy general leading two thousand troops to reinforce Shouyang—then one can secure Xu and Yu and aid the Si region.

units.zh: 其二曰：「一夫不耕，必有受其飢者。
units.en: Second: "When one farmer leaves his fields, someone goes hungry.
units.literal: The second said: "If one husband does not plow, there must be someone who suffers hunger.

units.zh: 今不耕之夫，動有萬計。
units.en: Tens of thousands of laborers now stand idle.
units.literal: Now husbands who do not plow move by tens of thousands.

units.zh: 春廢勸課之制，冬峻出租之令，下未見施，惟賦是聞。
units.en: Spring orders to promote farming are ignored; winter brings harsh rent demands—commoners hear only taxes, never relief.
units.literal: Spring abolishes the system of encouragement and inspection; winter harshly issues rent commands; below they do not see implementation, only hear levies.

units.zh: 賦不可以已，當思令百姓有以殷實。
units.en: Taxes cannot cease altogether, yet we must give the people means to become prosperous again.
units.literal: Levies cannot be stopped; one ought to think to cause the hundred surnames to have means to be abundant.

units.zh: 司徒置田曹掾，州一人，勸課農桑，察吏能否，今宜依舊置之。
units.en: Restore the Minister of Education's field clerks—one per province—to promote farming and sericulture and judge magistrates' performance, as in former times.
units.literal: The Minister of Works established Field Section aides, one per province, to encourage farming and sericulture and inspect officials' competence—now ought according to old establish them.

units.zh: 必得清恪奉公，足以宣示惠化者，則所益實弘矣。」
units.en: Choose men who are honest, diligent, and devoted to the public good; the gain will be immense."
units.literal: Must obtain those pure and respectful who serve the public, sufficient to declare and show kindly transformation—then the benefit is truly great.

units.zh: 其三曰：「諸外州郡將兵者及都督府非臨敵之軍，且田且守。
units.en: Third: "Commanders and area forces not engaged at the front should farm as they garrison.
units.literal: The third said: "Those who command troops in outer provinces and commanderies and area headquarters troops not facing the enemy—both farm and guard.

units.zh: 又先朝使五校出田，今四軍五校有兵者，及護軍所統外軍，可分遣二軍出，并屯要處。
units.en: Earlier courts sent the Five Camps to till the soil; detach two armies from the metropolitan forces and outer commands of the Guards to colonize strategic points.
units.literal: Moreover the former court sent the Five Camps out to farm; now the Four Armies and Five Camps that have troops, and outer armies commanded by the Guards—may divide and dispatch two armies out and jointly garrison key places.

units.zh: 緣江上下，皆有良田，開荒須一年之後即易。
units.en: Good land lies all along the Yangzi; one year of clearing fallow makes cultivation easy.
units.literal: Along the river up and down all have good fields; opening wasteland requires after one year then it is easy.

units.zh: 且軍人累重者在外，有樵採蔬食之人，於事為便。」
units.en: Soldiers long stationed abroad can gather fuel and greens on their own—a practical economy."
units.literal: Moreover soldiers burdened heavily being outside, having people who gather firewood and vegetables and eat—in affairs this is convenient.

units.zh: 其四曰：「建官以理世，不以私人也。
units.en: Fourth: "Offices exist to govern the realm, not to enrich private clients.
units.literal: The fourth said: "Establishing offices is to order the age—not for private persons.

units.zh: 如此則官寡而材精。
units.en: That keeps the bureaucracy lean and fills each post with able men.
units.literal: Thus offices would be few and talent refined.

units.zh: 周制六卿莅事，春秋之時，入作卿輔，出將三軍。
units.en: Under the Zhou the six grand ministers ran the government; in the Spring and Autumn era they rotated between court as chief counselors and the field as army commanders.
units.literal: The Zhou system had the six ministers discharge duties; in the Spring and Autumn period they entered to serve as ministerial aides and went out to command the three armies.

units.zh: 後代建官漸多，誠由事有煩簡耳。
units.en: Later ages piled on titles because some duties are heavy and others light.
units.literal: Later dynasties gradually multiplied offices, truly because tasks vary from intricate to simple.

units.zh: 然今江南六州之土，尚又荒殘，方之平日，數十分之一耳。
units.en: Yet the six southern provinces remain devastated—perhaps a tenth of their former productive land.
units.literal: But now the soil of the six provinces south of the Yangzi is still desolate and ruined; compared with ordinary times, it is only one-tenth in extent.

units.zh: 三省軍校無兵者，九府寺署可有并相領者，可有省半者，粗計閑劇，隨事減之。
units.en: Strip empty military slots from the three departments; merge overlapping bureaus of the nine ministries or cut their rolls in half; weigh idle against overburdened posts and abolish what you can.
units.literal: Among the three departments' military bureaus those without troops, and among the nine courts and directorates those that may be merged under joint heads or cut by half—roughly gauge which are idle and which pressing, and reduce offices accordingly.

units.zh: 荒殘之縣，或同在一城，可并合之。
units.en: Ruined counties that sit within one city wall should be consolidated.
units.literal: Desolate counties that share the same walled town may be amalgamated.

units.zh: 如此選既可精，祿俸可優，令足代耕，然後可責以清公耳。」
units.en: Tighter appointment lists allow richer salaries—pay men enough to live like landowners, then hold them to unstained public duty."
units.literal: Thus selection can be rigorous, stipends made ample, enough to replace income from plowing—only then may one demand pristine integrity.

units.zh: 其五曰：「古者親耕耤田以供粢盛，舊置耤田、廩犧之官。
units.en: Fifth: "Ancient kings tilled the sacred field themselves so the ancestral vessels would never lack grain; the old statutes created stewards for those fields and for the granary and sacrificial beasts.
units.literal: The fifth point: "In antiquity the sovereign personally plowed the ritual field to supply grain for sacrificial vessels; formerly there were officials for the ritual field and for the granary and victims.

units.zh: 今臨時市求，既上黷至敬，下費生靈，非所以虔奉宗廟蒸嘗之旨。
units.en: Buying grain on the open market profanes the highest ritual and bleeds the commoners—it is no way to honor the shrines with autumn and spring offerings.
units.literal: Now purchasing at the market on short notice both profanes supreme reverence above and wastes the living people below; it is not how to reverently observe the ancestral temples' steaming and tasting.

units.zh: 宜如舊制，立此二官。」
units.en: Restore the traditional offices for those two duties."
units.literal: It is fitting to restore the old system and establish these two offices."

units.zh: 其六曰：「使命愈遠，益宜得才，宣揚王化，延譽四方。
units.en: Sixth: "The farther an envoy travels, the abler he must be, for he carries the king's civilizing mandate and the court's reputation abroad.
units.literal: The sixth point: "The farther an envoy's mission, the more talent he needs—to proclaim royal transformation and extend reputation in every quarter.

units.zh: 人情不樂，遂取卑品之人，虧辱國命，生長患害。
units.en: No one wants the job, so petty men are sent—they disgrace the imperial charge and invite disaster.
units.literal: Because men dislike such assignments, mean-born persons are chosen; the state's mandate is shamed and harm is bred.

units.zh: 故宜重其選，不可減二千石見居二品者，」其七曰：「罪不相及，古之制也。
units.en: Raise the bar for envoys: do not demote candidates who already hold second rank at two thousand dan." Seventh: "Collective punishment was abolished in antiquity.
units.literal: Therefore the selection should be weighted heavily; one must not lower those ranked second among sitting two-thousand-dan officials." The seventh point: "Punishment does not extend to kin—that was the ancient rule.

units.zh: 近者大逆，誠由凶戾。
units.en: The recent rebellion sprang from vicious cruelty.
units.literal: Recent great treason truly arose from violent cruelty.

units.zh: 凶戾之甚，一時權用。
units.en: Harsh collective guilt was a wartime expedient.
units.literal: The utmost violence was a temporary expedient.

units.zh: 今遂施行，非聖朝之令典，宜如先朝除三族之制。」
units.en: To keep it on the books dishonors a civilized court—restore the earlier Jin rule that spared extended kin."
units.literal: Now to carry it on as permanent practice is not the code of a sage court; it is fitting to restore the former dynasty's abolition of punishment to three generations.

units.zh: 議奏，多納之。
units.en: The throne accepted most of his program.
units.literal: When the deliberation was memorialized, most of it was adopted.

units.zh: 帝疾篤，嶠與王導、郗鑒、庾亮、陸曄、卞壼等同受顧命。
units.en: The dying emperor entrusted Wen Jiao along with Wang Dao, Xi Jian, Yu Liang, Lu Ye, Bian Kun, and others with his final orders.
units.literal: When the emperor lay gravely ill, Jiao together with Wang Dao, Xi Jian, Yu Liang, Lu Ye, Bian Kun, and others jointly received the deathbed testament.

units.zh: 時歷陽太守蘇峻藏匿亡命，朝廷疑之。
units.en: Su Jun of Liyang was sheltering outlaws, and the court had begun to mistrust him.
units.literal: At the time Su Jun, Administrator of Liyang, harbored fugitives, and the court suspected him.

units.zh: 征西將軍陶侃有威名於荊楚，又以西夏為虞，故使嶠為上流形援。
units.en: Tao Kan, the general who guarded the west, was famed in Jing and Chu; fearing the northwestern frontier, the court stationed Wen Jiao upstream as his strategic reserve.
units.literal: General Who Conquers the West Tao Kan enjoyed martial renown in Jing and Chu, and because the western Xia frontier caused worry, Jiao was therefore sent as upstream support.

units.zh: 咸和初，代應詹為江州刺史、持節、都督、平南將軍，鎮武昌，甚有惠政，甄異行能，親祭徐孺子之墓。
units.en: Early in Xianhe he replaced Ying Zhan as governor of Jiangzhou, credential bearer, area commander, and General Who Pacifies the South, with headquarters at Wuchang. His rule was humane: he singled out able men and visited Xu Ruzi's grave to offer sacrifice himself.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Xianhe era he succeeded Ying Zhan as Governor of Jiangzhou, bearer of the credential, area commander, General Who Pacifies the South, garrisoned at Wuchang; he governed with benevolent policies, distinguishing talent and conduct, and personally sacrificed at the tomb of Xu Ruzi.

units.zh: 又陳豫章十郡之要，宜以刺史居之。
units.en: He urged that the ten Yuzhang commanderies were the region's pivot and deserved their own inspector.
units.literal: He also argued that the ten commanderies of Yuzhang formed a strategic knot and ought to be governed by an inspector.

units.zh: 尋陽濱江，都督應鎮其地。
units.en: Xunyang fronts the great river—an area commander should anchor there.
units.literal: Xunyang lies along the Yangzi; an area commander ought to hold that ground.

units.zh: 今以州帖府，進退不便。
units.en: Subordinating the province to the army command fouls every movement.
units.literal: Now having the province merely appended to the headquarters makes advance and retreat inconvenient.

units.zh: 且古鎮將多不領州，皆以文武形勢不同故也。
units.en: Frontier commanders once kept civil and military authority apart for good reason.
units.literal: Moreover ancient garrison commanders often did not also hold provincial authority, because civil and military priorities differ.

units.zh: 宜選單車刺史別撫豫章，專理黎庶。」
units.en: Send a lightweight provincial inspector to handle Yuzhang alone and mind the people.
units.literal: It is fitting to appoint a lone-chariot inspector separately to oversee Yuzhang and devote himself to the common people.

units.zh: 詔不許。
units.en: The emperor refused.
units.literal: The edict did not permit it.

units.zh: 在鎮見王敦畫像，曰：「敦大逆，宜加斲棺之戮，受崔杼之刑。
units.en: At his post he confronted Wang Dun's portrait and declared, "This traitor deserves his coffin split like a criminal's and the humiliation Cui Zhu dealt his corpse.
units.literal: While on duty he saw a portrait of Wang Dun and said: "Dun committed great treason; he deserves the punishment of having his coffin hacked open and should suffer the fate Cui Zhu inflicted.

units.zh: 古人闔棺而定諡，《春秋》大居正，崇王父之命，未有受戮於天子而圖形於群下。」
units.en: Antiquity sealed the coffin before fixing a posthumous name; the Spring and Autumn classics exalt legitimate rule—no man condemned by the emperor should hang in offices below."
units.literal: The ancients sealed the coffin before fixing the posthumous title; the Spring and Autumn Annals honor legitimate sovereignty and honor the mandate of the royal grandfather—never was one executed by the Son of Heaven yet pictured among subjects."

units.zh: 命削去之。
units.en: He had the likeness scraped away.
units.literal: He ordered it scraped away.

units.zh: 嶠聞蘇峻之徵也，慮必有變，求還朝以備不虞，不聽。
units.en: Learning that Su Jun had been summoned to the capital, Wen Jiao foresaw disaster and asked to return and guard against surprises; the court refused.
units.literal: When Jiao heard that Su Jun was being summoned, he feared trouble would follow and requested return to court to guard against the unexpected; permission was denied.

units.zh: 未幾而蘇峻果反。
units.en: Soon Su Jun rose in revolt.
units.literal: Before long Su Jun indeed rebelled.

units.zh: 嶠屯尋陽，遣督護王愆期、西陽太守鄧嶽、鄱陽內史紀瞻等率舟師赴難。
units.en: He camped at Xunyang and dispatched Wang Yanqi, Deng Yue of Xiyang, Ji Zhan of Poyang, and others with the river forces toward the capital.
units.literal: Jiao encamped at Xunyang and sent supervisor Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue, Administrator of Poyang Ji Zhan, and others leading a fleet to relieve the capital.

units.zh: 及京師傾覆，嶠聞之號慟。
units.en: News that the capital had fallen reached him in a storm of grief.
units.literal: When the capital fell, Jiao heard the news and wailed in grief.

units.zh: 人有候之者，悲哭相對。
units.en: Visitors found him weeping face to face with whoever entered.
units.literal: Those who came to console him wept together in sorrow.

units.zh: 俄而庾亮來奔，宣太后詔，進嶠驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司。
units.en: Yu Liang soon arrived as a fugitive bearing the empress dowager's order promoting Wen Jiao to general of agile cavalry with honors matching the Three Ducal Ministers.
units.literal: Shortly Yu Liang fled to him, proclaiming the empress dowager's edict, advancing Jiao to General of Agile Cavalry, chief with ceremony equal to the Three Offices.

units.zh: 嶠曰：「今日之急，殄寇為先，未效勳庸而逆受榮寵，非所聞也，何以示天下乎！」
units.en: Wen Jiao replied, "Annihilating the rebels comes first; taking glittering rewards before victory—such a thing is unheard of. What lesson would that teach the empire?"
units.literal: Jiao said: "Today's urgency is to destroy the bandits first; to accept lavish honors before merit is gained—I have not heard of such; how would it instruct the realm!"

units.zh: 固辭不受。
units.en: He steadfastly declined.
units.literal: He firmly declined and did not accept.

units.zh: 時亮雖奔敗，嶠每推崇之，分兵給亮。
units.en: Though Yu Liang had fled a defeated army, Wen Jiao continued to praise him and shared troops with him.
units.literal: Although Liang had fled in defeat, Jiao always praised him and divided troops to supply Liang.

units.zh: 遣王愆期等要陶侃同赴國難，侃恨不受顧命，不許。
units.en: He sent Wang Yanqi to coax Tao Kan into the coalition; Kan, bitter over being left out of the testament, would not budge.
units.literal: He sent Wang Yanqi and others to invite Tao Kan to join in saving the state; Kan, resentful that he had not received the deathbed charge, refused.

units.zh: 嶠初從之，後用其部將毛寶說，復固請侃行，語在寶傳。
units.en: Wen Jiao first accepted that answer, then took his officer Mao Bao's counsel and pressed Tao Kan again—as told in Mao Bao's memoir.
units.literal: At first Jiao yielded to this; later, adopting the advice of his officer Mao Bao, he again urgently requested Kan to march—the account is in Mao Bao's biography.

units.zh: 初，嶠與庾亮相推為盟主，嶠從弟充言於嶠曰：「征西位重兵彊，宜共推之。」
units.en: Wen Jiao and Yu Liang had each declined the coalition leadership until Wen Chong urged his cousin, "The western commander outranks us and commands the strongest host—yield the banner to him."
units.literal: At first Jiao and Yu Liang each urged the other to be covenant chief; Jiao's cousin Chong said to Jiao: "The general who guards the west holds heavy rank and strong troops—you ought jointly to defer to him."

units.zh: 嶠於是遣王愆期奉侃為盟主。
units.en: Wen Jiao then dispatched Wang Yanqi to install Tao Kan as alliance leader.
units.literal: Jiao thereupon sent Wang Yanqi to honor Kan as covenant chief.

units.zh: 侃許之，遣督護龔登率兵詣嶠。
units.en: Tao Kan agreed and sent Gong Deng with reinforcements to Wen Jiao's camp.
units.literal: Kan agreed and sent supervisor Gong Deng with troops to join Jiao.

units.zh: 嶠於是列上尚書，陳峻罪狀，有眾七千，灑泣登舟，移告四方征鎮曰：賊臣祖約、蘇峻同惡相濟，用生邪心。
units.en: Wen Jiao then memorialized the Secretariat with Su Jun's offenses, embarked seven thousand men in tears, and issued a call to arms to every provincial garrison: The traitors Zu Yue and Su Jun have abetted one another's wickedness and nursed treasonous designs.
units.literal: Jiao thereupon memorialized to the Secretariat enumerating Jun's crimes; he had seven thousand men, sprinkled tears as he boarded ship, and circulated a manifesto to the four quarters' commanders: The traitor ministers Zu Yue and Su Jun aided each other's evil and gave rise to perverse hearts.

units.zh: 天奪其魄，死期將至。
units.en: Heaven has abandoned their wits; their doom draws near.
units.literal: Heaven has seized their souls; the day of death approaches.

units.zh: 譴負天地，自絕人倫。
units.en: They have offended Heaven and Earth and severed themselves from humanity.
units.literal: They bear reproach before Heaven and Earth and cut themselves off from human bonds.

units.zh: 寇不可縱，宜增軍討撲，輒屯次湓口。
units.en: Rebels must not be spared—we should raise more troops to crush them; I have encamped at Chao Mouth.
units.literal: Bandits cannot be indulged; armies should be increased to strike them down; I have halted and encamped at Chao Mouth.

units.zh: 即日護軍庾亮至，宣太后詔，寇逼宮城，王旅撓敗，出告藩臣，謀寧社稷。
units.en: That day Yu Liang arrived bearing the empress dowager's edict: rebels had pressed the palace, the imperial army had been routed, and we now call on every frontier lord to save the realm.
units.literal: That very day Protector-General Yu Liang arrived and proclaimed the empress dowager's edict: the bandits pressed the palace city, the royal army was broken, and we appeal to the frontier lords to restore the altars of state.

units.zh: 後將軍郭默、冠軍將軍趙胤、奮武將軍龔保與嶠督護王愆期、西陽太守鄧嶽、鄱陽內史紀瞻，率其所領，相尋而至。
units.en: Rear General Guo Mo, Champion General Zhao Yin, Valiant Martial General Gong Bao, Wen Jiao's supervisor Wang Yanqi, Deng Yue of Xiyang, and Ji Zhan of Poyang brought their forces in succession.
units.literal: Rear General Guo Mo, Champion General Zhao Yin, Valiant Martial General Gong Bao, Jiao's supervisor Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue, and Administrator of Poyang Ji Zhan led their commands and arrived one after another.

units.zh: 逆賊肆凶，陵蹈宗廟，火延宮掖，矢流太極，二御幽逼，宰相困迫，殘虐朝士，劫辱子女。
units.en: The rebels rampaged through the ancestral shrines, set the palace ablaze, shot arrows into the Hall of Supreme Pole, drove both emperors into hiding, trapped the chief ministers, tortured court officials, and seized and abused women and children.
units.literal: The rebel bandits ran riot, trampled the ancestral temples, fire spread through the palace quarters, arrows flew at the Hall of Supreme Pole, both sovereigns were driven into peril, ministers were cornered, court officers were cruelly abused, and women and children were seized and shamed.

units.zh: 承問悲惶，精魂飛散。
units.en: Hearing this news, I am stricken with grief and terror; my soul itself seems scattered.
units.literal: Upon hearing this I grieve and panic; my spirit flies apart.

units.zh: 嶠闇弱不武，不能殉難，哀恨自咎，五情摧隕，慙負先帝託寄之重，義在畢力，死而後已。
units.en: I am untried in arms and failed to die with the capital; shame and remorse consume me. I bear the late emperor's heavy trust and am bound to give all I have until death.
units.literal: Jiao is dim and weak, not martial, and could not die in the crisis; grieving and blaming myself, my five emotions are shattered; ashamed of the late emperor's weighty trust, righteousness demands that I exhaust my strength until death.

units.zh: 今躬率所統，為士卒先，催進諸軍，一時電擊。
units.en: I now lead my own troops at the fore, pressing every army forward in one swift assault.
units.literal: Now I personally lead my command as vanguard of the soldiers, urging every army forward in a single lightning strike.

units.zh: 西陽太守鄧嶽、尋陽太守褚誕等連旗相繼，宣城內史桓彝已勒所屬屯濱江之要，江夏相周撫乃心求征，軍已向路。
units.en: Deng Yue of Xiyang, Chu Dan of Xunyang, and others marched with banners in train; Huan Yi of Xuancheng had already posted his men along the river; Zhou Fu of Jiangxia burned to join the campaign, and his troops were already marching.
units.literal: Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue, Administrator of Xunyang Chu Dan, and others followed with banners in succession; Administrator of Xuancheng Huan Yi had already mustered his men at the vital points along the river; Chancellor of Jiangxia Zhou Fu sought battle with all his heart, and his army was already on the road.

units.zh: 昔包胥楚國之微臣，重趼致誠，義感諸侯。
units.en: Long ago Shen Baoxu, a minor officer of Chu, blistered his feet pleading for aid and moved the feudal lords by sheer righteousness.
units.literal: In old days Shen Baoxu, a humble minister of Chu, blistered his feet in repeated appeals and moved the feudal lords by righteousness.

units.zh: 藺相如趙邦之陪隸，恥君之辱，按劍秦庭。
units.en: Lin Xiangru, a humble retainer of Zhao, drew his sword in the Qin court rather than endure his lord's shame.
units.literal: Lin Xiangru, a menial attendant of Zhao, shamed at his lord's humiliation, drew his sword in the Qin court.

units.zh: 皇漢之季，董卓作亂，劫遷獻帝，虐害忠良，關東州郡相率同盟。
units.en: At the fall of Han, Dong Zhuo seized the emperor and slaughtered the loyal; the eastern provinces rose in league.
units.literal: At the end of the Han house Dong Zhuo raised rebellion, seized and moved Emperor Xian, cruelly harmed the loyal and good, and the eastern provinces and commanderies joined in alliance one after another.

units.zh: 廣陵功曹臧洪，郡之小吏耳，登壇喢血，涕淚橫流，慷慨之節，實厲群后。
units.en: Zang Hong of Guangling was only a county clerk, yet he swore the blood oath with tears streaming—a spirit that truly roused the lords.
units.literal: Zang Hong, a minor clerk of Guangling, merely a petty officer of the commandery, ascended the altar and tasted blood, tears streaming—his ardent integrity truly stirred the lords.

units.zh: 况今居台鼎，據方州，列名邦，受國恩者哉！
units.en: How much more should those who now hold the highest offices, command provinces, and owe the state their rank!
units.literal: How much more those who now sit at the tripod of state, hold provincial commands, rank among famed domains, and receive the state's grace!

units.zh: 不期而會，不謀而同，不亦宜乎！
units.en: To gather without summons and unite without prior counsel—is this not only right!
units.literal: To meet without prior appointment and act as one without prior counsel—is this not fitting!

units.zh: 二賊合眾，不盈五千，且外畏胡寇，城內饑乏，後將軍郭默即於戰陣俘殺賊千人。
units.en: The two rebels together number fewer than five thousand; they fear barbarian raids without and hunger within, and Rear General Guo Mo has already killed a thousand of them in battle.
units.literal: The two bandits together do not exceed five thousand; moreover they fear the northern barbarians without and hunger and want within the city; Rear General Guo Mo has already captured and killed a thousand bandits on the battlefield.

units.zh: 賊今雖殘破都邑，其宿衛兵人即時出散，不為賊用。
units.en: Though the rebels have ravaged the capital, its palace guards have already fled and will not serve them.
units.literal: Though the bandits now ravage the capital, its palace guards have already scattered at once and are not used by the bandits.

units.zh: 且祖約情性褊阨，忌剋不仁，蘇峻小子，惟利是視，殘酷驕猜，權相假合。
units.en: Zu Yue is narrow, jealous, and cruel; Su Jun is a petty man who cares only for gain—cruel, arrogant, and suspicious, they merely use one another.
units.literal: Moreover Zu Yue's nature is narrow and harsh, jealous and unkind; Su Jun is a petty fellow who looks only to profit; cruel, arrogant, and suspicious, they merely borrow each other's strength.

units.zh: 江表興義，以抗其前，彊胡外寇，以躡其後，運漕隔絕，資食空懸，內乏外孤，勢何得久！
units.en: Loyal armies south of the Yangzi block them in front, barbarians harry them from behind, supply lines are severed, and provisions are exhausted—how can they last!
units.literal: Righteous armies rise south of the river to oppose them in front; strong barbarians raid from without to press them behind; transport routes are cut off and provisions hang empty; weak within and isolated without—how can their position endure!

units.zh: 群公征鎮，職在禦侮。
units.en: You commanders and frontier lords are charged with repelling invasion.
units.literal: You lords of expedition and command—the duty is to repel insult.

units.zh: 征西陶公，國之耆德，忠肅義正，勳庸弘著。
units.en: Lord Tao of the Western Expedition is the state's elder statesman—loyal, upright, and richly meritorious.
units.literal: Western Expeditionary Lord Tao is the state's elder in virtue, loyal, solemn, righteous, and upright, with grand and shining merit.

units.zh: 諸方鎮州郡咸齊斷金，同稟規略，以雪國恥，苟利社稷，死生以之。
units.en: Every frontier command and province stands united, sharing one plan to avenge the realm—life and death for the altars of state.
units.literal: Every frontier command, province, and commandery alike cuts gold as one, shares the same plan, to wash away the state's shame; if it profits the altars of soil and grain, life and death follow that cause.

units.zh: 嶠雖怯劣，忝據一方，賴忠賢之規，文武之助，君子竭誠，小人盡力，高操之士被褐而從戎，負薪之徒匍匐而赴命，率其私僕，致其私杖，人士之誠，竹帛不能載也。
units.en: Though I am unworthy in my command, with loyal counsel and civil and military aid, gentlemen give their all and common men their utmost—men of principle don coarse cloth for war and woodcutters crawl to answer the call, bringing private servants and weapons. Such devotion cannot be fully recorded.
units.literal: Though Jiao is timid and inferior, I disgracefully hold one region; relying on the counsel of the loyal and worthy and the aid of civil and military officers, gentlemen exhaust sincerity and common men give full strength; men of lofty conduct don coarse cloth to join the army and wood-bearers crawl forward to answer the call, leading private servants and bringing private weapons—the sincerity of officers and people bamboo and silk cannot record.

units.zh: 豈嶠無德而致之哉？
units.en: This is hardly because of my own virtue!
units.literal: How could Jiao's lack of virtue have brought this about!

units.zh: 士稟義風，人感皇澤。
units.en: Officers answer the call of righteousness; the people feel the emperor's grace.
units.literal: Officers receive the wind of righteousness; people feel the emperor's grace.

units.zh: 且護軍庾公，帝之元舅，德望隆重，率郭後軍、趙、龔三將，與嶠戮力，得有資憑，且悲且慶，若朝廷之不泯也。
units.en: Moreover Lord Yu the Protector-General, the emperor's senior maternal uncle, is eminent in virtue and renown; with Generals Guo, Zhao, and Gong he joins forces with me—we have real support, grieving yet rejoicing as though the court still stands.
units.literal: Moreover Protector-General Lord Yu, the emperor's senior maternal uncle, is weighty in virtue and renown; leading Generals Guo, Zhao, and Gong of the rear army, he joins strength with Jiao—we have support to rely on, grieving yet rejoicing as though the court were not yet extinguished.

units.zh: 其各明率所統，無後事機。
units.en: Let each of you lead your forces clearly and do not delay.
units.literal: Let each clearly lead what you command and do not delay the moment.

units.zh: 賞募之信，明如日月。
units.en: Rewards and bounties are pledged as bright as sun and moon.
units.literal: The faith of rewards and bounties is bright as sun and moon.

units.zh: 有能斬約峻者，封五等侯，賞布萬匹。
units.en: Whoever slays Zu Yue or Su Jun shall be made a fifth-rank marquis and rewarded with ten thousand bolts of cloth.
units.literal: Whoever can behead Yue or Jun shall be enfeoffed as marquis of the fifth rank and rewarded with ten thousand bolts of cloth.

units.zh: 夫忠為令德，為仁由己，萬里一契，義不在言也。
units.en: Loyalty is the highest virtue; duty rests on each man's will. Though we are far apart, our bond is one—righteousness needs no further words.
units.literal: Loyalty is the foremost virtue; benevolence depends on oneself; though ten thousand li apart we share one bond—righteousness needs no further words.

units.zh: 時陶侃雖許自下而未發，復追其督護龔登。
units.en: Tao Kan had promised to lead the march himself but still delayed, even summoning Gong Deng back.
units.literal: At the time although Tao Kan had agreed to come south himself he had not yet set out, and again recalled his supervisor Gong Deng.

units.zh: 嶠重與侃書曰：僕謂軍有進而無退，宜增而不可減。
units.en: Wen Jiao wrote Tao Kan another letter: I hold that armies advance and never retreat—they should be augmented, not cut.
units.literal: Jiao wrote again to Kan: Your servant holds that an army should advance and not retreat—it ought to be increased and cannot be reduced.

units.zh: 近已移檄遠近，言於盟府，剋後月半大舉。
units.en: I have already sent proclamations far and wide and told the alliance headquarters that a major campaign is set for the middle of next month.
units.literal: Recently I have circulated proclamations near and far and reported to the alliance headquarters that a great campaign is set for the middle of next month.

units.zh: 南康、建安、晉安三郡軍並在路次，同赴此會，惟須仁公所統至，便齊進耳。
units.en: The armies of Nankang, Jian'an, and Jin'an are already marching to this rendezvous; we need only your forces to arrive and we can advance together.
units.literal: The armies of the three commanderies Nankang, Jian'an, and Jin'an are all on the road, coming together to this rendezvous; we need only wait for the forces my lord Ren commands to arrive, and then we advance together.

units.zh: 仁公今召軍還，疑惑遠近，成敗之由，將在於此。
units.en: But you now recall your troops—this sows doubt near and far, and success or failure may turn on it.
units.literal: My lord Ren now recalls the army—this confuses near and far; the cause of success or failure will lie here.

units.zh: 僕才輕任重，實憑仁公篤愛，遠稟成規。
units.en: My talent is slight for so heavy a charge; I truly rely on your deep regard and follow your settled plan from afar.
units.literal: Your servant's talent is light and burden heavy; I truly rely on my lord Ren's deep affection and take distant counsel from your settled plan.

units.zh: 至於首啟戎行，不敢有辭，僕與仁公當如常山之蛇，首尾相衛，又脣齒之喻也。
units.en: As for opening the campaign first, I dare not refuse; you and I should be like the serpent of Mount Changshan, head and tail guarding each other—the very image of lips and teeth.
units.literal: As for being first to open the campaign, I dare not refuse; your servant and my lord Ren should be like the serpent of Mount Changshan, head and tail guarding each other—the metaphor of lips and teeth as well.

units.zh: 恐惑者不達高旨，將謂仁公緩於討賊，此聲難追。
units.en: I fear the confused will not grasp your intent and will say you are slow to punish the rebels—such talk, once spread, is hard to recall.
units.literal: I fear the confused will not grasp your high intent and will say my lord Ren is slow to punish the bandits—such talk is hard to recall.

units.zh: 僕與仁公並受方嶽之任，安危休慼，理既同之。
units.en: You and I alike bear regional command; our safety, danger, joy, and sorrow are naturally shared.
units.literal: Your servant and my lord Ren alike bear the charge of a regional mountain; safety and danger, joy and sorrow—reason already makes them the same.

units.zh: 且自頃之顧，綢繆往來，情深義重，著於人士之口，一旦有急，亦望仁公悉眾見救，況社稷之難！
units.en: Moreover our close exchanges of late are known to every officer and man; in any crisis I hope you will bring all your forces to aid me—how much more in a crisis of the altars of state!
units.literal: Moreover since recent times our careful exchanges have been deep in feeling and heavy in righteousness, known in the mouths of officers and people; once there is urgency, I also hope my lord Ren will bring all your forces to rescue—how much more in the state's crisis!

units.zh: 惟僕偏當一州，州之文武莫不翹企。
units.en: I alone hold this province, and every civil and military officer in it stands in eager expectation.
units.literal: Only your servant alone holds one province; the civil and military of the province none fail to stand on tiptoe in expectation.

units.zh: 假令此州不守，約峻樹置官長於此，荊楚西逼彊胡，東接逆賊，因之以饑饉，將來之危乃當甚於此州之今日也。
units.en: If this province falls and Zu Yue and Su Jun set up officials here, Jing and Chu will face strong barbarians in the west and rebels in the east; with famine added, the danger ahead will exceed today's crisis.
units.literal: If this province cannot be held and Yue and Jun establish officials here, Jing and Chu will press the strong barbarians in the west and meet rebel bandits in the east; with famine added, future peril will be far worse than this province's present day.

units.zh: 以大義言之，則社稷顛覆，主辱臣死，公進當為大晉之忠臣，參桓文之義，開國承家，銘之天府；
units.en: In great righteousness the altars are overturned and ministers die when their lord is shamed; if you advance you will be a loyal minister of Jin, sharing the cause of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, ennobling your house and inscribing your name in Heaven's records;
units.literal: Speaking in terms of great righteousness, the altars of state are overturned and when the lord is shamed the minister dies; if my lord advances you should be a loyal minister of Great Jin, sharing the righteousness of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, founding states and inheriting houses, inscribed in the celestial treasury;

units.zh: 退當以慈父雪愛子之痛。
units.en: if you retreat you should, as a loving father, ease a beloved son's grief.
units.literal: if you retreat you should as a loving father wipe away a beloved son's pain.

units.zh: 約峻凶逆無道，囚制人士，裸其五形。
units.en: Zu Yue and Su Jun are savage rebels who imprison officers and people and strip them naked.
units.literal: Yue and Jun are fierce, rebellious, and without the Way; they imprison and control officers and people and strip their five forms bare.

units.zh: 近日來者，不可忍見。
units.en: What the refugees report is unbearable to witness.
units.literal: Those who have come recently cannot be endured to see.

units.zh: 骨肉生離，痛感天地，人心齊一，咸皆切齒。
units.en: Families are torn apart; grief moves Heaven and Earth; every heart is united in rage.
units.literal: Flesh and bone are torn apart while living; grief touches Heaven and Earth; hearts are united as one and all gnash their teeth.

units.zh: 今之進討，若以石投卵耳！
units.en: Today's campaign would be like casting stones at eggs!
units.literal: Today's advance to punish them is like casting stone at egg!

units.zh: 今出軍既緩，復召兵還，人心乖離，是為敗於幾成也。
units.en: You have already moved slowly and now recall your troops; hearts will turn away—this is defeat snatched from the brink of victory.
units.literal: Now the army goes out slowly and troops are recalled again; hearts turn apart—this is defeat on the verge of success.

units.zh: 願深察所陳，以副三軍之望。
units.en: I beg you to weigh what I have said and answer the army's hopes.
units.literal: I wish you to examine deeply what I have stated and answer the three armies' hope.

units.zh: 峻時殺侃子瞻，由是侃激勵，遂率所統與嶠、亮同赴京師，戎卒六萬，旌旗七百餘里，鉦鼓之聲震於百里，直指石頭，次于蔡洲。
units.en: Su Jun had executed Tao Kan's son Tao Zhan, which finally galvanized Kan. He brought his army with Wen Jiao and Yu Liang toward the capital—sixty thousand men, seven hundred li of banners, drums audible for a hundred li—bearing down on Stone City and anchoring at Cai Isle.
units.literal: At that time Jun had killed Kan's son Zhan; therefore Kan was roused and led his own forces together with Jiao and Liang toward the capital—sixty thousand soldiers, banners stretching seven hundred li, drum and gong shaking the hundred-li plain, pointing straight at Stone Fortress, halting at Cai Isle.

units.zh: 侃屯查浦，嶠屯沙門浦。
units.en: Tao Kan camped at Zha Creek; Wen Jiao at Shamen Creek.
units.literal: Kan encamped at Zha Pu; Jiao encamped at Shamen Pu.

units.zh: 時祖約據歷陽，與峻為首尾，見嶠等軍盛，謂其黨曰：「吾本知嶠能為四公子之事，今果然矣。」
units.en: Zu Yue held Liyang in tandem with Su Jun. Seeing Wen Jiao's host, he told his officers, "I knew Wen Jiao could pull together the great coalition—now he has."
units.literal: At the time Zu Yue held Liyang, coordinating with Jun head and tail; seeing Jiao and others' army strong, he said to his followers: "I always knew Jiao could do what the four lords did—now it proves true."

units.zh: 峻聞嶠將至，逼大駕幸石頭。
units.en: Su Jun, hearing of Wen Jiao's approach, marched the emperor to Stone Fortress.
units.literal: When Jun heard Jiao was about to arrive, he forced the imperial carriage to go to Stone Fortress.

units.zh: 時峻軍多馬，南軍杖舟楫，不敢輕與交鋒。
units.en: Su Jun's men were cavalry-heavy; the southern allies stuck to their boats and hesitated to engage.
units.literal: At the time Jun's army had many horses; the southern army relied on boats and dared not lightly join battle.

units.zh: 用將軍李根計，據白石築壘以自固，使庾亮守之。
units.en: They adopted Li Gen's plan: seize White Rock, throw up walls, and put Yu Liang in charge.
units.literal: Following General Li Gen's plan, they seized White Rock and built ramparts to secure themselves, assigning Yu Liang to defend them.

units.zh: 賊步騎萬餘來攻，不下而退，追斬二百餘級。
units.en: Ten thousand rebel horse and foot assaulted the walls without success and fled; the allies killed over two hundred in pursuit.
units.literal: Enemy infantry and cavalry over ten thousand attacked but failed to take it and withdrew; two hundred-odd heads were taken in pursuit.

units.zh: 嶠又於四望磯築壘以逼賊，曰：「賊必爭之，設伏以逸待勞，是制賊之一奇也。」
units.en: Wen Jiao threw up another bastion at Siwang Jetty to pinch the rebels. "They will fight for this ground," he said—set an ambush and let eager fatigue—classic bait.
units.literal: Jiao again built a fort at Siwang Jetty to press the bandits, saying: "The bandits will contest this—lay an ambush and wait at ease for their fatigue; it is one outstanding stratagem against them."

units.zh: 是時義軍屢戰失利，嶠軍食盡，陶侃怒曰：「使君前云不憂無將士，惟得老僕為主耳。
units.en: The loyalists kept losing; Wen Jiao's supplies ran out. Tao Kan growled, "You insisted you needed no talent beyond this old man as figurehead.
units.literal: At that time the loyalist army repeatedly fought and lost; Jiao's army ran out of food; Tao Kan angrily said: "The governor formerly said he did not worry about lacking officers and men—only needed this old servant as chief.

units.zh: 今數戰皆北，良將安在？
units.en: Every battle goes wrong—where are these splendid generals now?
units.literal: Now several battles have all gone north—where are the good generals?

units.zh: 荊州接胡蜀二虜，倉廩當備不虞，若復無食，僕便欲西歸，更思良算。
units.en: Jingzhou borders barbarians west and Shu south—the granaries must stay full. Starve us again and I march home to rethink.
units.literal: Jingzhou borders the two foes Hu and Shu; the granaries ought to guard against emergency; if again there is no food, I shall wish to return west and rethink the plan.

units.zh: 但今歲計，殄賊不為晚也。」
units.en: Still, we can finish the bandits this year if we hold firm."
units.literal: But this year's reckoning—destroying the bandits is not too late."

units.zh: 嶠曰：「不然。
units.en: Wen Jiao answered, "Not so.
units.literal: Jiao said: "It is not so.

units.zh: 自古成監，師克在和。
units.en: History shows victorious armies march in harmony.
units.literal: From antiquity the lesson of success is that the army conquers through harmony.

units.zh: 光武之濟昆陽，曹公之拔官渡，以寡敵眾，杖義故也。
units.en: Emperor Guangwu took Kunyang; Cao Cao took Guandu—both beat bigger hosts because justice was theirs.
units.literal: Guangwu's rescue of Kunyang, Cao Cao's victory at Guandu—using the few against the many, they leaned on righteousness.

units.zh: 峻、約小豎，為海內所患，今日之舉，決在一戰。
units.en: Su Jun and Zu Yue are rabble hated across the realm—this war turns on a single clash.
units.literal: Jun and Yue are petty fellows, a scourge within the seas; today's undertaking will be settled in one battle.

units.zh: 峻勇而無謀，藉驕勝之勢，自謂無前，今挑之戰，可一鼓而擒也。
units.en: Su Jun is fierce yet witless, drunk on victory—taunt him into the open and one assault bags him.
units.literal: Jun is brave but lacks stratagem; relying on arrogant momentum of victory, he deems himself unstoppable—now provoke him to battle and he can be seized in one drum-roll.

units.zh: 奈何捨垂立之功，設進退之計！
units.en: Why throw away a winning stroke for wavering plans?
units.literal: How abandon a victory within reach and indulge schemes of advance and retreat!

units.zh: 且天子幽逼，社稷危殆，四海臣子，肝腦塗地，嶠等與公並受國恩，是致命之日，事若克濟，則臣主同祚，如其不捷，身雖灰滅，不足以謝責於先帝。
units.en: The emperor is penned and imperiled; the altars totter. Every loyal subject would die for the throne. Wen Jiao and you alike owe everything to the state—this is the hour to spend your lives. Victory lifts ruler and minister together; defeat reduces us to ash still owing the late emperor an apology.
units.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven is confined and imperiled; altars and grain hang in peril; subjects within the four seas would lay down liver and brains on the ground—Jiao and others together with my lord received the state's grace; this is the day to devote life; if the affair succeeds, lord and ministers share fortune alike; if not, though bodies turn to ash and dust, it is not enough to apologize to the late emperor.

units.zh: 今之事勢，義無旋踵，騎猛獸，安可中下哉！
units.en: Duty leaves no retreat—you ride a tiger midway.
units.literal: In the present situation, duty allows no turning back; riding a fierce beast—how can one dismount halfway!

units.zh: 公若違眾獨反，人心必沮。
units.en: Withdraw alone against every ally and you break every heart.
units.literal: If my lord alone turns back against the host, men's hearts will surely sink.

units.zh: 沮眾敗事，義旗將廻指於公矣。」
units.en: Broken morale loses the war—and the allies' spears turn on you."
units.literal: When hearts sink affairs fail; the banner of righteousness will wheel and point at my lord.

units.zh: 侃無以對，遂留不去。
units.en: Tao Kan had no reply and stayed.
units.literal: Kan had nothing to answer and therefore stayed and did not leave.

units.zh: 嶠於是創建行廟，廣設壇場，告皇天后土祖宗之靈，親讀祝文，聲氣激揚，流涕覆面，三軍莫能仰視。
units.en: Wen Jiao raised a field shrine, spread the ritual arena, and prayed to Heaven, Earth, and the imperial ancestors, reading the invocation himself until his voice cracked and tears masked his face—soldiers could not lift their eyes.
units.literal: Jiao thereupon founded a traveling shrine, broadly set up altar precincts, announced to August Heaven, august Earth, and the spirits of the ancestors, personally reading the prayer text; his voice rose fierce and bright, tears streaming over his face—the three armies none could look up at him.

units.zh: 其日侃督水軍向石頭，亮、嶠等率精勇一萬從白石以挑戰。
units.en: That day Tao Kan drove the fleet toward Stone City while Yu Liang, Wen Jiao, and ten thousand elite troops sortied from White Rock.
units.literal: That day Kan supervised the water force toward Stone Fortress; Liang, Jiao, and others led ten thousand picked warriors from White Rock to offer battle.

units.zh: 時峻勞其將士，因醉，突陣馬躓，為侃將所斬，峻弟逸及子碩嬰城自固。
units.en: Su Jun was feasting his troops, rode out drunk, fell from his horse, and Tao Kan's men killed him. His brother Su Yi and son Su Shuo locked themselves inside.
units.literal: At the time Jun was toasting his officers; drunk, he charged the line; his horse stumbled and he was cut down by Kan's officer; Jun's younger brother Yi and son Shuo held the city fast.

units.zh: 嶠乃立行臺，布告天下，凡故吏二千石、臺郎御史以下，皆令赴臺。
units.en: Wen Jiao opened a field headquarters and summoned every former two-thousand-dan official and Secretariat clerk to rally there.
units.literal: Jiao then set up a mobile headquarters, proclaimed to the realm that all former officials of two-thousand-dan rank and Secretariat and censorial clerks down should report to headquarters.

units.zh: 於是至者雲集。
units.en: They came in clouds.
units.literal: Thereupon arrivals gathered like clouds.

units.zh: 司徒王導因奏嶠、侃錄尚書，遣間使宣旨，並讓不受。
units.en: Wang Dao petitioned to name Wen Jiao and Tao Kan recording secretaries; secret messengers carried the order—both refused.
units.literal: Minister of Education Wang Dao therefore memorialized Jiao and Kan as recording secretaries; secret envoys bore the edict—both declined.

units.zh: 賊將匡術以臺城來降，為逸所擊，求救於嶠。
units.en: The turncoat Kuang Shu offered the palace quarter but Su Yi attacked him; he begged Wen Jiao for relief.
units.literal: Rebel general Kuang Shu surrendered the palace quarter but was struck by Yi and sought rescue from Jiao.

units.zh: 江州別駕羅洞曰：「今水暴長，救之不便，不如攻榻杭。
units.en: Luo Dong of Jiangzhou said, "The flood tide makes rescue risky—strike the Ta-hang bastion instead.
units.literal: Jiangzhou aide Luo Dong said: "Now the waters have swollen suddenly; rescue is awkward—it is better to strike Ta-hang.

units.zh: 榻杭軍若敗，術圍自解。」
units.en: Crush that garrison and Kuang Shu's trap springs open."
units.literal: If the Ta-hang army is defeated, Shu's siege lifts of itself.

units.zh: 嶠從之，遂破賊石頭軍。
units.en: Wen Jiao agreed and smashed Su Jun's army at Stone City.
units.literal: Jiao followed this and thereupon broke the enemy army at Stone Fortress.

units.zh: 奮威長史滕含抱天子奔于嶠船。
units.en: Teng Han of the Swift Might staff carried the emperor into Wen Jiao's boat.
units.literal: Swift Might senior clerk Teng Han bore the Son of Heaven in his arms to Jiao's ship.

units.zh: 時陶侃雖為盟主，而處分規略一出於嶠，及賊滅，拜驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，封始安郡公，邑三千戶。
units.en: Although Tao Kan titled himself alliance chief, Wen Jiao shaped every plan. After victory he became general of agile cavalry with Three Ducal honors, plus attendant cavalry regular, enfeoffed duke of Shi'an at three thousand households.
units.literal: Although at the time Tao Kan was covenant chief, disposition and strategy all proceeded from Jiao; when the bandits were destroyed, Jiao was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, chief with ceremony equal to the Three Offices, additionally Attendant Cavalry Regular, enfeoffed Duke of Shi'an commandery, three thousand households.

units.zh: 初，峻黨路永、匡術、賈寧中途悉以眾歸順，王導將褒顯之，嶠曰：「術輩首亂，罪莫大焉。
units.en: Early on Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning had defected with their troops; Wang Dao meant to honor them until Wen Jiao said, "Those men began the revolt—the crime could not be greater.
units.literal: At first Jun's followers Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning midway all surrendered their hosts to allegiance; Wang Dao was about to reward them; Jiao said: "Shu and company began the rebellion—no crime was greater.

units.zh: 晚雖改悟，未足以補前失。
units.en: Belated repentance cannot erase that guilt.
units.literal: Though late they changed understanding, it is not enough to redeem earlier fault.

units.zh: 全其首領，為幸己過，何可復寵授哉！」
units.en: Letting them keep their heads was mercy enough—never reward them."
units.literal: Sparing their heads was already fortune enough—how again enrich them with offices!

units.zh: 導無以奪。
units.en: Wang Dao yielded.
units.literal: Dao had nothing to overrule him.

units.zh: 朝議將留輔政，嶠以導先帝所任，固辭還藩。
units.en: The court wanted Wen Jiao to stay as regent; he insisted Wang Dao held the late emperor's trust and returned to his Jiangzhou command.
units.literal: Court deliberation proposed retaining him to assist governance; Jiao held that Dao had been employed by the late emperor and firmly declined to return to his provincial command.

units.zh: 復以京邑荒殘，資用不給，嶠借資蓄，具器用，而後旋于武昌，至牛渚磯，水深不可測，世云其下多怪物，嶠遂燬犀角而照之。
units.en: The capital remained ruined and broke, so Wen Jiao borrowed provisions and gear before sailing back to Wuchang. At Niuzhu Jetty the depths were immeasurable—folk said monsters lurked below—so he burned rhinoceros horn to light the river.
units.literal: Again because the capital wastes were desolate and supplies insufficient, Jiao borrowed stores and furnished equipment, then rotated back to Wuchang; reaching Niuzhu Jetty, the water was deep beyond measuring—the world said below were many monsters; Jiao therefore burned rhinoceros horn to shine through it.

units.zh: 須臾，見水族覆火，奇形異狀，或乘馬車著赤衣者。
units.en: Momentarily he saw river beings draped in fire—grotesque shapes, some in red riding horse-drawn carts.
units.literal: In a moment he saw aquatic creatures shielding flame, strange shapes and forms, some riding horse-drawn cars in red garments.

units.zh: 嶠其夜夢人謂己曰：「與君幽明道別，何意相照也？」
units.en: That night he dreamed a voice said, "We belong to separate realms—why burn light upon us?"
units.literal: That night Jiao dreamed someone told him: "You and I part by dark and bright roads—why do you shine a light on me?"

units.zh: 意甚惡之。
units.en: The omen sickened him.
units.literal: The intention was very sinister.

units.zh: 嶠先有齒疾，至是拔之，因中風，至鎮未旬而卒，時年四十二。
units.en: Plagued by toothache, he had the teeth pulled and suffered a stroke; he died within ten days of reaching post, forty-two years old.
units.literal: Jiao previously had tooth ailment; thereupon he extracted them and suffered a wind stroke; reaching headquarters within ten days he died, aged forty-two.

units.zh: 江州士庶聞之，莫不相顧而泣。
units.en: Every household in Jiangzhou wept when they heard.
units.literal: Gentry and commoners of Jiangzhou hearing it none failed to look at one another and weep.

units.zh: 帝下冊書曰：「朕以眇身，纂承洪緒，不能光闡大道，化洽時雍，至乃狂狡滔天，社稷危逼。
units.en: The emperor's edict read, "We inherit a vast mandate yet failed to spread the Way or pacify the times—rebels ran riot and the throne tottered.
units.literal: The emperor issued a patent of enfeoffment: "We, of slight person, inherit the great line; unable to broadly manifest the great Way and harmonize the age in timely peace—thereupon the violent and cunning overflowed Heaven, altars and grain imperiled.

units.zh: 惟公明鑒特達，識心經遠，懼皇綱之不維，忿凶寇之縱暴，唱率群后，五州響應，首啟戎行，元惡授馘。
units.en: You alone foresaw danger, roused the provinces, and marched first—the chief rebel lost his head.
units.literal: Only my lord bright insight special penetration, mind versed in the distant, feared the royal net would not hold, resented the fierce bandits' wanton cruelty, led the host of lords—five provinces echoed—and first raised the army's march; the chief evil yielded his head.

units.zh: 王室危而復安，三光幽而復明，功格宇宙，勳著八表。
units.en: You restored the house and brought back the sun, moon, and stars—your merit fills heaven and earth.
units.literal: The royal house was perilous yet restored safe; the three luminaries were dark yet bright again; merit spans the cosmos, achievement shines through the eight quarters.

units.zh: 方賴大猷以拯區夏，天不憖遺，早世薨殂，朕用痛悼于厥心。
units.en: We looked to your counsel to save the heartland, yet Heaven stole you—Our grief is boundless.
units.literal: Just relying on your great plan to save the central plains, Heaven shows no kindness and leaves you not; you departed early in death; We use pain and grief in Our heart.

units.zh: 夫褒德銘勳，先王之明典，今追贈公侍中、大將軍、持節、都督、刺史，公如故，賜錢百萬，布千匹，諡曰忠武，祠以太牢。」
units.en: The kings of old honored merit—we posthumously add palace attendant, grand general, credential, area command, and governor; your ducal rank stands; grant cash and silk; posthumous name Loyal and Martial; sacrifice with the grand victim."
