units.literal: To praise virtue and inscribe achievement is the enlightened code of former kings; now We posthumously award my lord Palace Attendant, Grand General, bearer of credential, area commander, governor—duke as before, grant one hundred million cash, one thousand bolts of cloth, posthumous title Loyal and Martial, sacrifice with grand ox, sheep, and pig.

units.zh: 初葬于豫章，後朝廷追嶠勳德，將為造大墓於元明二帝陵之北，陶侃上表曰：「故大將軍嶠忠誠著於聖世，勳義感于人神，非臣筆墨所能稱陳。
units.en: He was first buried in Yuzhang. Court artisans later planned a mausoleum north of Emperors Yuan and Ming until Tao Kan memorialized, "The late Wen Jiao's loyalty outshone his age; words fail his service.
units.literal: At first buried in Yuzhang; later the court, remembering Jiao's merit and virtue, was about to build a great tomb north of the Yuan and Ming emperors' tombs; Tao Kan submitted a memorial: "The late Grand General Jiao's loyalty shone in the sage age; merit and righteousness moved men and spirits—not something your subject's brush can declare.

units.zh: 臨卒之際，與臣書別，臣藏之篋笥，時時省視，每一思述，未嘗不中夜撫膺，臨飯酸噎。
units.en: His deathbed letter to me still sits in my chest—I read it nights and clutch my breast; meals stick in my throat.
units.literal: At the moment of death he bade farewell to your subject in a letter; your subject stores it in a box and from time to time inspects it—each time thinking of it, never failing to clutch his breast at midnight, choke over meals with sour grief.

units.zh: '人之云亡'，嶠實當之。
units.en: As the ode runs, "When good men vanish from the world"—that line was written for Wen Jiao.
units.literal: The ode says 'when fine men pass away'—Jiao truly embodies it.

units.zh: 謹寫嶠書上呈，伏惟陛下既垂御省，傷其情旨，死不忘忠，身沒黃泉，追恨國恥，奬臣戮力，救濟艱難，使亡而有知，抱恨結草，豈樂今日勞費之事。
units.en: He copied Wen Jiao's letter to the throne: even beyond death Wen Jiao burned to redeem national shame and urged Tao Kan onward—ghost or man, he would scorn empty pageantry over his bones.
units.literal: I respectfully transcribe Jiao's letter for presentation; humbly I trust Your Majesty will peruse it and be moved by its intent—forgetting not loyalty even in death, body laid in the yellow springs yet still regretting the nation's shame, urging your servant to strain every nerve through hardship—if the dead may know, they would knot grass in gratitude—how could they desire today's costly undertaking.

units.zh: 願陛下慈恩，停其移葬，使嶠棺柩無風波之危，魂靈安於后土。」
units.en: He begged the emperor to cancel the grand reburial so Wen Jiao's coffin need not brave the rivers and his shade could rest undisturbed."
units.literal: I wish Your Majesty in kindness and grace halt the removal for reburial, so Jiao's coffin faces no peril on the waves and his soul rests easy beneath the soil.

units.zh: 詔從之。
units.en: The emperor granted the petition.
units.literal: The edict followed this.

units.zh: 其後嶠後妻何氏卒，子放之便載喪還都。
units.en: After Wen Jiao's second wife Lady He died, Wen Fangzhi convoyed both cortèges to Jiankang.
units.literal: Later Jiao's second wife Lady He died; his son Fangzhi then carried both coffins back to the capital.

units.zh: 詔葬建平陵北，幷贈嶠前妻王氏及何氏始安夫人印綬。
units.en: The court buried them north of Jianping Ling and posthumously titled Wen Jiao's first wife Lady Wang and Lady He as ladies of Shi'an with full insignia.
units.literal: An edict ordered burial north of Jianping Mausoleum and additionally invested Jiao's former wife Lady Wang and Lady He as Ladies of Shi'an with seals and ribbons.

units.zh: 放之嗣爵，少歷清官，累至給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: Wen Fangzhi inherited the dukedom, rose through respectable posts, and reached attendant gentleman at the palace gates.
units.literal: Fangzhi inherited the noble rank; in youth he served in pure offices, rising to Gentleman at Yellow Gates.

units.zh: 以貧，求為交州，朝廷許之。
units.en: Poor official pay drove him to ask for Jiaozhou; the throne agreed.
units.literal: Because of poverty he requested Jiaozhou; the court permitted it.

units.zh: 王述與會稽王牋曰：「放之溫嶠之子，宜見優異，而投之嶺外，竊用愕然。
units.en: Wang Shu warned the Prince of Kuaiji: "Wen Fangzhi is Wen Jiao's heir—he deserves favor, not exile beyond the mountains.
units.literal: Wang Shu wrote to the Prince of Kuaiji: "Fangzhi is Wen Jiao's son—he ought to receive generous treatment—yet we cast him beyond the ranges—I am privately stunned.

units.zh: 願遠存周禮，近參人情，則望實惟允。」
units.en: Balance distant precedent from the Zhou against plain humanity—that would satisfy both honor and sense."
units.literal: I wish distantly to preserve the Zhou rites, near at hand to consult human feeling—then reputation and substance will match.

units.zh: 時竟不納。
units.en: The advice went nowhere.
units.literal: At the time it was ultimately not adopted.

units.zh: 放之既至南海，甚有威惠。
units.en: Once he reached Nanhai he ruled with firm justice and mercy.
units.literal: After Fangzhi reached Nanhai he wielded authority and kindness.

units.zh: 將征林邑，交阯太守杜寶、別駕阮朗並不從，放之以其沮眾，誅之，勒兵而進，遂破林邑而還。
units.en: He planned a strike on Linyi; Du Bao of Jiaozhi and aide Ruan Lang balked—he executed them for mutiny, marched, crushed Linyi, and sailed home.
units.literal: When about to campaign against Linyi, Administrator of Jiaozhi Du Bao and aide Ruan Lang both refused to obey; Fangzhi because they dampened morale executed them, mobilized troops and advanced, thereupon defeated Linyi and returned.

units.zh: 卒于官。
units.en: He died in post.
units.literal: He died in office.

units.zh: 弟式之，新建縣侯，位至散騎常侍。
units.en: His brother Wen Shizhi held the marquisate of Xinjian and became attendant cavalry regular.
units.literal: His younger brother Shizhi was Marquis of Xinjian county and rose to Attendant Cavalry Regular.

units.zh: 郗鑒
units.en: Xi Jian.
units.literal: Xi Jian.

units.zh: 郗鑒，字道徽，高平金鄉人，漢御史大夫慮之玄孫也。
units.en: Xi Jian of Jinxiang in Gaoping—courtesy Daohui—descended from the Han imperial counselor Xi Lu.
units.literal: Xi Jian, courtesy name Daohui, was a man of Jinxiang in Gaoping, great-great-grandson of Imperial Counselor Lu of Han.

units.zh: 少孤貧，博覽經籍，躬耕隴畝，吟詠不倦。
units.en: He grew up poor and fatherless but devoured the canon, tilled his own fields, and never tired of poetry and song.
units.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he broadly read the classics, personally plowed the fields, chanting and reciting tireless.

units.zh: 以儒雅著名，不應州命。
units.en: Scholars praised his cultivation; he ignored appointments from the province.
units.literal: He was famed as a Confucian gentleman and did not answer provincial summons.

units.zh: 趙王倫辟為掾，知倫有不臣之迹，稱疾去職。
units.en: Prince Zhao Lun offered him a staff post; seeing Lun's treasonous ambitions, he resigned on grounds of illness.
units.literal: Prince Zhao Lun summoned him as aide; knowing Lun bore tokens of disloyalty, he pleaded illness and left office.

units.zh: 及倫篡，其黨皆至大官，而鑒閉門自守，不染逆節。
units.en: When Sima Lun seized the throne his followers climbed to power; Xi Jian barred his doors and kept clean of the coup.
units.literal: When Lun usurped, his clique all rose to high office, yet Jian shut his gate and kept himself pure, stained by no rebellion.

units.zh: 惠帝反正，參司空軍事，累遷太子中舍人、中書侍郎。
units.en: After Emperor Hui returned, Xi Jian joined the minister of works' staff and rose to secretary and palace attendant to the heir.
units.literal: When Emperor Hui was restored, Jian joined the Minister of Works' military staff, rising through Palace Junior in the Heir's Household and Secretariat Gentleman.

units.zh: 東海王越辟為主簿，舉賢良，不行。
units.en: Sima Yue of Donghai named him chief clerk and nominated him as "worthy and good"; he declined.
units.literal: Prince Donghai Sima Yue summoned him as chief clerk; recommended as Worthy and Good—he did not take office.

units.zh: 征東大將軍苟晞檄為從事中郎。
units.en: Gou Xi, general who conquered the east, summoned him as senior clerk.
units.literal: General Who Conquers the East Gou Xi summoned him by proclamation as senior clerk.

units.zh: 晞與越方以力爭，鑒不應其召。
units.en: Gou Xi and Sima Yue were at war; Xi Jian ignored the call.
units.literal: Xi and Yue were then locked in struggle for power; Jian did not answer the summons.

units.zh: 從兄旭，晞之別駕，恐禍及己，勸之赴召，鑒終不廻，晞亦不之逼也。
units.en: His cousin Xi Xu—Gou Xi's aide—feared for himself and urged compliance; Xi Jian still refused, yet Gou Xi did not press him.
units.literal: His cousin Xu, Xi's aide, fearing disaster reaching himself, urged him to obey the summons; Jian never turned back; Xi also did not force him.

units.zh: 及京師不守，寇難鋒起，鑒遂陷於陳午賊中。
units.en: When Luoyang fell and rebels multiplied, Xi Jian fell captive to Chen Wu's gang.
units.literal: When the capital did not hold and bandit calamities sprang like spear-points, Jian thereupon fell among Chen Wu's bandit band.

units.zh: 邑人張實先求交於鑒，鑒不許。
units.en: A neighbor, Zhang Shi, had courted his friendship before; Xi Jian rejected him.
units.literal: Townsmen Zhang Shi earlier sought friendship with Jian; Jian refused.

units.zh: 至是，實於午營來省鑒疾，既而卿鑒。
units.en: Zhang Shi then visited him sick in Chen Wu's camp and presumed upon familiarity.
units.literal: Thereupon Zhang from Wu's camp came to inquire after Jian's illness; afterward he addressed Jian with undue familiarity.

units.zh: 鑒謂實曰：「相與邦壤，義不及通，何可怙亂至此邪！」
units.en: Xi Jian told him, "We were neighbors yet never exchanged courtesy—how dare you exploit rebellion to force intimacy!"
units.literal: Jian said to Shi: "We share neighboring soil yet courtesy never brought us together—how dare you rely on chaos to reach this point!

units.zh: 實大慙而退。
units.en: Zhang Shi withdrew in shame.
units.literal: Shi was greatly ashamed and withdrew.

units.zh: 午以鑒有名於世，將逼為主，鑒逃而獲免。
units.en: Chen Wu meant to make the celebrated Xi Jian his figurehead; Xi Jian escaped.
units.literal: Wu because Jian had fame in the world was about to force him to be chief; Jian fled and escaped.

units.zh: 午尋潰散，鑒得歸鄉里。
units.en: Chen Wu's band soon dissolved and Xi Jian went home.
units.literal: Wu soon scattered and collapsed; Jian was able to return to his village.

units.zh: 于時所在饑荒，州中之士素有感其恩義者，相與資贍。
units.en: Famine stalked the region, yet local scholars who remembered his decency pooled supplies for him.
units.literal: At that time famine raged everywhere; gentlemen of the province who long felt his kindness and righteousness together supplied him.

units.zh: 鑒復分所得，以賉宗族及鄉曲孤老，賴而全濟者甚多，咸相謂曰：「今天子播越，中原無伯，當歸依仁德，可以後亡。」
units.en: He shared the gifts with kinsmen and destitute neighbors. Many survived thanks to him. They said, "The emperor is a refugee and the heartland lacks a lord—only humane leadership offers shelter."
units.literal: Jian again divided what he received to relieve his lineage and village orphans and elders; many relied on him and were wholly saved—all said together: "Now the Son of Heaven wanders lost; no protector holds the central plain—we ought to attach to humane virtue and may survive afterward.

units.zh: 遂共推鑒為主，舉千餘家俱避難於魯之嶧山。
units.en: They chose Xi Jian as their leader and moved more than a thousand households to Yi Mountain in Lu for safety.
units.literal: Thereupon together they pushed Jian as chief; over a thousand households jointly fled hardship to Yi Mountain in Lu.

units.zh: 元帝初鎮江左，承制假鑒龍驤將軍、兗州刺史，鎮鄒山。
units.en: When Sima Rui secured the south, he named Xi Jian interim general of the soaring dragon and inspector of Yanzhou at Zou Mountain.
units.literal: When the Yuan Emperor first garrisoned the Yangzi's left bank, acting on imperial mandate he appointed Jian acting General of Soaring Dragon and Inspector of Yanzhou, garrisoned at Zou Mountain.

units.zh: 時荀藩用李述，劉琨用兄子演，並為兗州，各屯一郡，以力相傾，闔州編戶，莫知所適。
units.en: Xun Fan backed Li Shu while Liu Kun backed his nephew Liu Yan—both claimed Yanzhou, split garrisons, and wrestled for households who had nowhere to turn.
units.literal: At the time Xun Fan employed Li Shu and Liu Kun employed his nephew Liu Yan—both as inspectors of Yanzhou, each encamping in one commandery, striving by force against each other; registered households of the whole province knew nowhere to turn.

units.zh: 又徐龕、石勒左右交侵，日尋干戈，外無救援，百姓饑饉，或掘野鼠蟄燕而食之，終無叛者。
units.en: Xu Kan and Shi Le pressed from both sides without relief; people ate dormice and cave swallows—yet none deserted Xi Jian.
units.literal: Moreover Xu Kan and Shi Le harried left and right; daily they sought arms; outside there was no rescue; common people starved—some dug field rats and hibernating swallows to eat—yet in the end none rebelled.

units.zh: 三年間，眾至數萬。
units.en: In three years his host numbered tens of thousands.
units.literal: Within three years the multitude reached several tens of thousands.

units.zh: 帝就加輔國將軍、都督兗州諸軍事。
units.en: The prince promoted him to general who supports the state and area commander for Yanzhou.
units.literal: The emperor additionally invested him General Who Supports the State and Area Commander of Yanzhou military affairs.

units.zh: 永昌初，徵拜領軍將軍，既至，轉尚書，以疾不拜。
units.en: Early in Yongchang he was recalled as colonel of the guards; transferred to secretary but declined on grounds of illness.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yongchang he was summoned as Colonel of the Garrison Army; having arrived, he was transferred to Secretary—because of illness he did not accept.

units.zh: 時明帝初即位，王敦專制，內外危逼，謀杖鑒為外援，由是拜安西將軍、兗州刺史、都督揚州江西諸軍、假節，鎮合肥。
units.en: Emperor Ming faced Wang Dun's dictatorship and stationed Xi Jian west as general who pacifies the west, inspector of Yanzhou, area commander from the Yangzi westward—with credential and headquarters at Hefei.
units.literal: At the time Emperor Ming had newly ascended; Wang Dun monopolized power; internal and external peril pressed—the plot leaned on Jian as outer support; therefore he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yanzhou, Area Commander of Jiangxi military affairs south of Yangzhou, acting credential, garrisoned at Hefei.

units.zh: 敦忌之，表為尚書令，徵還。
units.en: Wang Dun envied him and engineered his recall as director of state affairs.
units.literal: Dun envied him and memorialized him as Director of the Department of State Affairs, summoning him back.

units.zh: 道經姑孰，與敦相見，敦謂曰：「樂彥輔短才耳。
units.en: At Gushu Wang Dun sneered, "Yue Guang is second-rate.
units.literal: Passing through Gushu he met Dun; Dun said to him: "Yue Yanfu is but minor talent.

units.zh: 後生流宕，言違名檢，考之以實，豈勝滿武秋邪？」
units.en: Those gifted youngsters break every rule—tell me how Yue Guang outranks Man Yi."
units.literal: Later youths drift dissolute; speech violates name and scrutiny—examining by facts, how could he surpass Man Wuqiu?

units.zh: 鑒曰：「擬人必于其倫。
units.en: Xi Jian replied, "Compare like with like.
units.literal: Jian said: "When comparing men one must match kind.

units.zh: 彥輔道韻平淡，體識沖粹，處傾危之朝，不可得而親疏。
units.en: Yue Guang moves through a dangerous court with serene detachment—neither push nor pull him off balance.
units.literal: Yanfu's Dao charm is placid and plain; his substance and insight are limpid and pure; in a tottering court one cannot draw him near or push him far.

units.zh: 及愍懷太子之廢，可謂柔而有正。
units.en: When they cashiered Crown Prince Minhuai he remained gentle yet principled.
units.literal: At the deposition of Crown Prince Minhuai he may be called yielding yet upright.

units.zh: 武秋失節之士，何可同日而言！」
units.en: Man Yi broke his oath—no comparison."
units.literal: Wuqiu is a man who lost integrity—how may they be spoken of the same day!

units.zh: 敦曰：「愍懷廢徙之際，交有危機之急，人何能以死守之乎！
units.en: Wang Dun shot back, "During that crisis who could die on principle?
units.literal: Dun said: "At the deposition and exile of Minhuai, mutually there was crisis acute—how could men guard it with death!

units.zh: 以此相方，其不減明矣。」
units.en: Then Yue Guang shines brighter."
units.literal: Using this to compare squarely, his inferiority is clear.

units.zh: 鑒曰：「丈夫既潔身北面，義同在三，豈可偷生屈節，靦顏天壤邪！
units.en: Xi Jian said, "A man who serves the throne upholds the three bonds—he does not cling to life and betray honor.
units.literal: Jian said: "A gentleman having purified himself to serve the north face, duty joins the Three Bonds—how may he steal life and bend his integrity, shame-faced between Heaven and earth!

units.zh: 苟道數終極，固當存亡以之耳。」
units.en: When fate ends, you accept survival or ruin with it."
units.literal: If the Dao's reckoning reaches its end, indeed one should live or die by it.

units.zh: 敦素懷無君之心，聞鑒言，大忿之，遂不復相見，拘留不遣。
units.en: Wang Dun—who already disdained emperors—raged at that speech, refused further audiences, and held Xi Jian hostage.
units.literal: Dun always harbored a heart without a lord; hearing Jian's words he greatly resented him; then would no longer meet him and detained him without sending him away.

units.zh: 敦之黨與譖毀日至，鑒舉止自若，初無懼心。
units.en: While Wang Dun's clique daily maligned him, Xi Jian stayed calm and afraid of nothing.
units.literal: Dun's faction daily spread slander; Jian's bearing remained composed—at first no fear.

units.zh: 敦謂錢鳳曰：「郗道徽儒雅之士，名位既重，何得害之！」
units.en: He told Qian Feng, "Xi Jian is a scholar of stature—we cannot murder him."
units.literal: Dun said to Qian Feng: "Xi Daohui is a Confucian gentleman; name and position are already weighty—how could we harm him!

units.zh: 乃放還臺。
units.en: He released Xi Jian to return to the capital.
units.literal: Thereupon he was released to return to the metropolitan apparatus.

units.zh: 鑒遂與帝謀滅敦。
units.en: Xi Jian then joined Emperor Ming to plot Wang Dun's destruction.
units.literal: Jian thereupon with the emperor plotted to destroy Dun.

units.zh: 既而錢鳳攻逼京都，假鑒節，加衛將軍、都督從駕諸軍事。
units.en: When Qian Feng struck the capital, Xi Jian received a credential as general who guards the army and commander of escort forces.
units.literal: Soon Qian Feng attacked and pressed the capital; Jian was lent a credential, additionally General Who Guards the Army, Area Commander of military affairs attending the imperial carriage.

units.zh: 鑒以無益事實，固辭不受軍號。
units.en: He refused the extra titles as pointless ornament.
units.literal: Jian held it brought no benefit to the facts and firmly declined, not accepting the military title.

units.zh: 時議者以王含、錢鳳眾力百倍，苑城小而不固，宜及軍勢未成，大駕自出距戰。
units.en: Advisers said Wang Han and Qian Feng outnumbered the court a hundredfold and the palace walls were weak—the emperor should sortie before rebel lines hardened.
units.literal: At the time debaters held that Wang Han and Qian Feng's forces were a hundredfold stronger, the park wall small and not firm—it was fitting while their military momentum was not yet formed for the great carriage himself to go out and resist battle.

units.zh: 鑒曰：「群逆縱逸，其勢不可當，可以算屈，難以力競。
units.en: Xi Jian answered, "Those traitors run wild; blunt force will not stop them—only strategy bends them.
units.literal: Jian said: "The mass of rebels runs rampant; their momentum cannot be stopped—it may be bent by stratagem, hard to compete by force.

units.zh: 且含等號令不一，抄盜相尋，百姓懲往年之暴，皆人自為守。
units.en: Wang Han's officers disagree; they loot each other's turf; civilians still recall last year's terror and defend every lane.
units.literal: Moreover Han and others' commands are not uniform; raiding and pillaging follow one another; common people chastened by prior years' cruelty each man guards himself.

units.zh: 乘逆順之勢，何往不剋！
units.en: Ride the moral high ground and every blow lands.
units.literal: Riding the momentum of wrong versus right—where would you not conquer!

units.zh: 且賊無經略遠圖，惟恃豕突一戰，曠日持久，必啟義士之心，令謀猷得展。
units.en: The rebels have no grand plan—only a desperate rush. Drag the fight out and loyal hearts awaken; plans get room to work.
units.literal: Moreover the bandits lack long-range strategy; they rely only on a boar-charge single battle; prolonged days and enduring time will surely awaken righteous warriors' hearts and let stratagems unfold.

units.zh: 今以此弱力敵彼彊寇，決勝負於一朝，定成敗於呼吸，雖有申胥之徒，義存投袂，何補於既往哉！」
units.en: Pit this exhausted host against fresh rebels in one reckless day—even Shen Xu could not salvage disaster."
units.literal: Now with this weak strength to oppose that strong bandit, deciding victory or defeat in one morning, fixing success or failure in a breath—though there were men like Shen Xu, righteousness stored in casting aside sleeves—what help for what is past!

units.zh: 帝從之。
units.en: The emperor agreed.
units.literal: The emperor followed this.

units.zh: 鑒以尚書令領諸屯營。
units.en: Xi Jian, as director of state affairs, coordinated every camp.
units.literal: Jian as Director of State Affairs commanded all encampments.

units.zh: 及鳳等平，溫嶠上議，請宥敦佐吏，鑒以為先王崇君臣之教，故貴伏死之節；
units.en: After Qian Feng fell, Wen Jiao urged leniency for Wang Dun's staff; Xi Jian countered that ancient kings prized ministers who died for their lord.
units.literal: When Feng and others were pacified, Wen Jiao submitted a proposal requesting amnesty for Dun's clerks; Jian held that former kings honored the teaching of lord and minister, therefore prized the integrity of dying prostrate;

units.zh: 昏亡之主，故開待放之門。
units.en: They granted clemency only to hopeless sovereigns.
units.literal: For benighted perishing lords therefore they opened gates awaiting release.

units.zh: 王敦佐吏雖多逼迫，然居逆亂之朝，無出關之操，準之前訓，宜加義責。
units.en: Wang Dun's aides chose to serve a usurper—protocol demands blame even if coercion existed.
units.literal: Although Wang Dun's aides were mostly coerced, yet dwelling in a rebellious court they lacked the integrity to leave office—measuring by former instruction, righteous blame should be applied.

units.zh: 又奏錢鳳母年八十，宜蒙全宥。
units.en: He separately asked mercy for eighty-year-old Lady Qian, Qian Feng's mother.
units.literal: He also memorialized Qian Feng's mother was eighty years old and ought to receive full pardon.

units.zh: 乃從之。
units.en: The throne accepted both lines.
units.literal: Thereupon it was followed.

units.zh: 封高平侯，賜絹四千八百匹。
units.en: They enfeoffed him marquis of Gaoping with forty-eight hundred bolts of silk.
units.literal: Enfeoffed Marquis of Gaoping, granted four thousand eight hundred bolts of silk.

units.zh: 帝以其有器望，萬機動靜輒問之，乃詔鑒特草上表疏，以從簡易。
units.en: Emperor Ming consulted him on every decision and told him to draft memorials in plain language.
units.literal: The emperor because he had capacity and prestige—every movement of the myriad affairs constantly consulted him—thereupon issued an edict Jian especially to draft memorials and petitions following simplicity.

units.zh: 王導議欲贈周札官，鑒以為不合，語在札傳。
units.en: Wang Dao wanted posthumous honors for Zhou Zha; Xi Jian objected—the story sits in Zhou Zha's memoir.
units.literal: Wang Dao deliberated wishing to posthumously award Zhou Zha office; Jian held it improper—the account is in Zha's biography.

units.zh: 導不從。
units.en: Wang Dao ignored him.
units.literal: Dao did not follow.

units.zh: 鑒於是駮之曰：「敦之逆謀，履霜日久，緣札開門，令王師不振。
units.en: Xi Jian shot back: "Wang Dun's rebellion had ripened for years—Zhou Zha opened Stone City and shattered morale.
units.literal: Jian thereupon refuted him saying: "Dun's treasonous plot walked on frost long accumulated; because Zha opened the gate it made the royal army fail to rally.

units.zh: 若敦前者之舉，義同桓文，則先帝可為幽厲邪？」
units.en: If that coup matched Duke Huan or Duke Wen, were our late emperors tyrants You and Li?"
units.literal: If Dun's earlier action matched righteousness with Huan and Wen, could the late emperor then be You or Li!

units.zh: 朝臣雖無以難，而不能從。
units.en: Nobody refuted him on the floor yet Dao's faction still blocked him.
units.literal: Court ministers though had nothing to refute him, yet could not follow.

units.zh: 俄而遷車騎將軍、都督徐兗青三州軍事、兗州刺史、假節，鎮廣陵。
units.en: Soon he became general of chariots and cavalry, area commander over Xu, Yan, and Qing, inspector of Yanzhou with credential, headquartered at Guangling.
units.literal: Shortly he was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Area Commander of Xu Yan Qing three provinces' military affairs, Inspector of Yanzhou, acting credential, garrisoned at Guangling.

units.zh: 尋而帝崩，鑒與王導、卞壼、溫嶠、庾亮、陸曄等並受遺詔，輔少主，進位車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍。
units.en: When Emperor Ming died, Xi Jian joined Wang Dao, Bian Kun, Wen Jiao, Yu Liang, and Lu Ye as guardians of the boy emperor—promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry with Three Ducal honors and attendant cavalry regular.
units.literal: Soon the emperor died; Jian together with Wang Dao, Bian Kun, Wen Jiao, Yu Liang, Lu Ye, and others jointly received the testamentary edict, assisting the young sovereign; advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, chief with ceremony equal to the Three Offices, additionally Attendant Cavalry Regular.

units.zh: 咸和初，領徐州刺史。
units.en: Early in Xianhe he added inspector of Xuzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xianhe he concurrently held Inspector of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 及祖約、蘇峻反，鑒聞難，便欲率所領東赴。
units.en: Zu Yue and Su Jun rose; Xi Jian meant to march east the moment he heard.
units.literal: When Zu Yue and Su Jun rebelled, Jian hearing the calamity wished to lead what he commanded east to rescue.

units.zh: 詔以北寇不許。
units.en: Northern raiders kept him pinned—imperial orders forbade the march.
units.literal: An edict because of northern foes did not permit.

units.zh: 於是遣司馬劉矩領三千人宿衛京都。
units.en: He sent aide Liu Ju with three thousand men to reinforce Jiankang.
units.literal: Thereupon he sent Major Liu Ju leading three thousand men to night-garrison the capital.

units.zh: 尋而王師敗績，矩遂退還。
units.en: The imperial army collapsed and Liu Ju fell back.
units.literal: Soon the royal army was routed; Ju thereupon withdrew and returned.

units.zh: 中書令庾亮宣太后口詔，進鑒為司空。
units.en: Yu Liang relayed the empress dowager's oral instruction promoting Xi Jian to minister of works.
units.literal: Director of the Secretariat Yu Liang proclaimed the empress dowager's oral edict, advancing Jian to Minister of Works.

units.zh: 鑒去賊密邇，城孤糧絕，人情業業，莫有固志，奉詔流涕，設壇場，刑白馬，大誓三軍曰：「賊臣祖約、蘇峻不恭天命，不畏王誅，凶戾肆逆，干國之紀，陵汩五常，侮弄神器，遂制脅幽主，拔本塞原，殘害忠良，禍虐黎庶，使天地神祇靡所依歸。
units.en: Xi Jian stood beside the enemy: isolated city, empty granaries, terrified men. Weeping, he raised an altar, slew a white horse, and swore the army: "Zu Yue and Su Jun defy Heaven and the throne—rebellious, brutal, traitorous—they hold the emperor hostage, uproot the dynasty, slaughter loyal ministers, and ravage the people until gods and earth turn away.
units.literal: Jian was close to the bandits, the city isolated and grain cut off, human hearts fearful—none had firm resolve; receiving the edict he wept, set up altar precincts, slew a white horse, and greatly swore the three armies: "The traitorous ministers Zu Yue and Su Jun do not revere Heaven's mandate, do not fear royal punishment—vicious and cruel they rebel and violate the state's norms; they insult the five constants and toy with the sacred vessels; then controlling and coercing the secluded lord, uprooting trunk and blocking source, they mutilate the loyal and good and scourge the black-haired people, causing Heaven and Earth and the spirits nowhere to turn for reliance.

units.zh: 是以率土怨酷，兆庶泣血，咸願奉辭罰罪，以除元惡。
units.en: The realm groans; every household bleeds tears—we march to execute those monsters.
units.literal: Therefore within the realm resentment is bitter, omens and commoners weep blood—all wish to offer words punishing crime and remove the chief evil.

units.zh: 昔戎狄泯周，齊桓糾盟；
units.en: When barbarians destroyed Zhou, Duke Huan of Qi rallied the lords.
units.literal: In old days the Rong and Di extinguished Zhou; Duke Huan of Qi rallied the covenant;

units.zh: 董卓陵漢，群后致討。
units.en: When Dong Zhuo seized Luoyang, every prince raised troops.
units.literal: Dong Zhuo insulted Han; the host of lords mobilized punishment.

units.zh: 義存君親，古今一也。
units.en: Duty to sovereign and father binds every age alike.
units.literal: Righteousness rests in serving lord and kin—ancient and modern are one.

units.zh: 今主上幽危，百姓倒懸，忠臣正士志存報國。
units.en: Our emperor lies imprisoned; the people hang head-down; every loyal heart burns to serve.
units.literal: Now the lord above is confined in peril; common people hang inverted; loyal ministers and upright gentlemen harbor minds to repay the state.

units.zh: 凡我同盟，既盟之後，戮力一心，以救社稷。
units.en: Who swear here today owe one another single-minded devotion to the throne.
units.literal: All who share our covenant—after alliance—join strength single-hearted to rescue altars and grain.

units.zh: 若二寇不梟，義無偷安。
units.en: Until both rebels fall we dare not rest.
units.literal: If the two bandits are not beheaded, righteousness allows no stealing ease.

units.zh: 有渝此盟，明神殛之！」
units.en: Break this oath and Heaven kills you."
units.literal: Who violates this covenant—bright spirits strike him dead!

units.zh: 鑒登壇慷慨，三軍爭為用命。
units.en: Xi Jian mounted the altar in blazing zeal; every regiment clamored for orders.
units.literal: Jian ascended the altar passionate and stirring; the three armies vied to obey commands.

units.zh: 乃遣將軍夏侯長等間行，謂平南將軍溫嶠曰：「今賊謀欲挾天子東入會稽，宜先立營壘，屯據要害，既防其越逸，又斷賊糧運，然後靜鎮京口，清壁以待賊。
units.en: He sent Xia Houzhang by stealth to tell Wen Jiao: "The rebels mean to drag the emperor east toward Kuaiji—throw up camps on choke points first to stop their flight and their supplies, then hold Jingkou with cleared fields until they starve.
units.literal: He then sent General Xia Houzhang and others by secret routes, saying to General Who Pacifies the South Wen Jiao: "Now the bandits plot to seize the Son of Heaven and move east into Kuaiji—it is fitting first to erect camps and garrison critical points—both guarding against their leap away and cutting bandit grain transport—then calmly secure Jingkou with clear walls awaiting the bandits.

units.zh: 賊攻城不拔，野無所掠，東道既斷，糧運自絕，不過百日，必自潰矣。」
units.en: They cannot breach the walls or forage; cut their eastern line and their supplies die—in under a hundred days they unravel."
units.literal: If the bandits cannot storm the city they plunder nothing in the wilds; once the eastern road is cut grain runs out—in less than a hundred days they must collapse of themselves.

units.zh: 嶠深以為然。
units.en: Wen Jiao agreed wholeheartedly.
units.literal: Jiao deeply approved this.

units.zh: 及陶侃為盟主，進鑒都督揚州八郡軍事。
units.en: Once Tao Kan led the alliance, Xi Jian took charge of eight Yangzhou jurisdictions.
units.literal: When Tao Kan became covenant chief, Jian was advanced Area Commander of military affairs for eight Yangzhou commanderies.

units.zh: 時撫軍將軍王舒、輔軍將軍虞潭皆受鑒節度，率眾渡江，與侃會于茄子浦。
units.en: Wang Shu and Yu Tan crossed the river under Xi Jian's command and linked up with Tao Kan at Eggplant Creek.
units.literal: At the time General Who Pacifies the Army Wang Shu and General Who Supports the Army Yu Tan both received Jian's orders, leading hosts across the Yangzi and joining Kan at Eggplant Ford.

units.zh: 鑒築白石壘而據之。
units.en: Xi Jian fortified White Rock and held the ridge.
units.literal: Jian built White Rock fortress and held it.

units.zh: 會舒、潭戰不利，鑒與後將軍郭默還丹徒，立大業、曲阿、庱亭三壘以距賊。
units.en: After Wang Shu and Yu Tan lost ground, Xi Jian and Guo Mo pulled back to Dantu and threw up Daye, Qu'e, and Dingting to block the rebels.
units.literal: When Shu and Tan fought unsuccessfully, Jian together with Rear General Guo Mo returned to Dantu, erecting three fortresses—Daye, Qu'e, and Dingting—to block the bandits.

units.zh: 而賊將張健來攻大業，城中乏水，郭默窘迫，遂突圍而出，三軍失色。
units.en: Zhang Jian stormed Daye; water ran dry; Guo Mo broke out in disgrace—the army went pale with shock.
units.literal: But bandit officer Zhang Jian came to attack Daye; the city lacked water; Guo Mo was pressed tight and burst the encirclement to escape—the three armies lost color.

units.zh: 參軍曹納以為大業京口之扞，一旦不守，賊方軌而前，勸鑒退還廣陵以俟後舉。
units.en: Staff officer Cao Na argued Daye shielded Jingkou—lose it and rebels pour through—and urged retreat to Guangling.
units.literal: Aide Cao Na held that Daye was Jingkou's shield—if lost in one morning the bandits advance abreast; he urged Jian to withdraw to Guangling and await a later move.

units.zh: 鑒乃大會僚佐，責納曰：「吾蒙先帝厚顧，荷託付之重，正復捐軀九泉不足以報。
units.en: Xi Jian summoned his officers and rebuked Cao Na: "The late emperor favored me beyond desert—I owe him my bones.
units.literal: Jian thereupon greatly convened aides and reproached Na: "I received deep favor from the late emperor and shoulder heavy trust—even casting away corpse in the nine springs would not repay.

units.zh: 今彊寇在郊，眾心危迫，君腹心之佐，而生長異端，當何以率先義眾，鎮一三軍邪！」
units.en: Strong rebels besiege us—how dare my chief strategist preach panic!"
units.literal: Now strong bandits ring the suburbs and every heart quakes—you are aide of belly and heart yet breed dissent—how shall you lead the righteous host and steady the three armies!

units.zh: 將斬之，久而乃釋。
units.en: He ordered execution, then relented after an agonizing delay.
units.literal: He was about to execute him; after long time then released him.

units.zh: 會峻死，大業圍解。
units.en: Su Jun's death lifted the siege of Daye.
units.literal: When Jun died the siege of Daye lifted.

units.zh: 及蘇逸等走吳興，鑒遣參軍李閎追斬之，降男女萬餘口。
units.en: Xi Jian sent Li Hong after Su Yi's remnants and accepted ten thousand captives.
units.literal: When Su Yi and others fled toward Wuxing, Jian sent aide Li Hong to pursue and behead them; over ten thousand male and female surrendered.

units.zh: 拜司空，加侍中，解八郡都督，更封南昌縣公，以先爵封其子曇。
units.en: They named him minister of works and palace attendant, trimmed his military belt to routine duties, made him duke of Nanchang, and passed his old title to Xi Tan.
units.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works, additionally Palace Attendant, relieved of eight-commandery command, enfeoffed Duke of Nanchang county, investing his former noble rank on his son Tan.

units.zh: 時賊帥劉徵聚眾數千，浮海抄東南諸縣。
units.en: Rebel leader Liu Zheng harried the coast with thousands of followers.
units.literal: At the time bandit chief Liu Zheng gathered a host of several thousand, sailing the sea to raid southeastern counties.

units.zh: 鑒遂城京口，加都督揚州之晉陵吳郡諸軍事，率眾討平之。
units.en: Xi Jian fortified Jingkou, commanded Jinling and Wu, and crushed Liu Zheng.
units.literal: Jian thereupon walled Jingkou, additionally appointed Area Commander of Jinling and Wu commanderies of Yangzhou, leading hosts to pacify them.

units.zh: 進位太尉。
units.en: He rose to grand commandant.
units.literal: He was promoted to Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 後以寢疾，上疏遜位曰：「臣疾彌留，遂至沈篤，自忖氣力，差理難冀。
units.en: Bedridden, he offered his resignation: "Recovery looked impossible.
units.literal: Later because of bedridden illness he submitted a memorial yielding office: "Your servant's illness lingers and sinks ever deeper; judging my strength, recovery is hard to hope.

units.zh: 有生有死，自然之分。
units.en: Life and death follow nature's law.
units.literal: There is birth and there is death—the division of nature.

units.zh: 但忝位過才，會無以報，上慙先帝，下愧日月。
units.en: He had never matched his titles—shaming throne and time alike.
units.literal: Only I disgrace my position beyond my talent; never have I repaid it—above I shame the late emperor, below I shame sun and moon.

units.zh: 伏枕哀歎，抱恨黃泉。
units.en: He nursed guilt toward the grave.
units.literal: Leaning on pillow I mourn and sigh, harboring regret toward the yellow springs.

units.zh: 臣今虛乏，救命朝夕，輒以府事付長史劉遐，乞骸骨歸丘園。
units.en: He handed headquarters to Liu Xia and asked leave to retire home.
units.literal: Your servant now is hollow and exhausted, preserving life morning and evening; therefore hand headquarters affairs to Senior Clerk Liu Xia and beg bones returned to hill and garden.

units.zh: 惟願陛下崇山海之量，弘濟大猷，任賢使能，事從簡易，使康哉之歌復興於今，則臣雖死，猶生之日耳。
units.en: He prayed the throne would magnify its counsel, trust talent, and rule simply—then his death would feel like life.
units.literal: Only I wish Your Majesty embrace the capacity of mountain and sea, broadly rescue the great plan, appoint the worthy and employ the able, handling affairs with simplicity—cause the song of peace again to rise today—then though your servant dies it is as living days.

units.zh: 臣所統錯雜，率多北人，或逼遷徙，或是新附，百姓懷土，皆有歸本之心。
units.en: His troops were northern refugees who still longed for home.
units.literal: Those your servant commands are mixed—mostly northerners—some driven to migrate, some newly attached; common people cherish their soil—all bear minds to return home.

units.zh: 臣宣國恩，示以好惡，處與田宅，漸得少安。
units.en: He had settled them with fields and patience.
units.literal: Your servant proclaimed state grace, showed them good and evil, settled them with fields and houses—gradually they gained slight peace.

units.zh: 聞臣疾篤，眾情駭動，若當北渡，必啟寇心。
units.en: News of his collapse might stampede them north into enemy arms.
units.literal: Hearing your servant's illness is grave, mass hearts are shaken—if they should cross north they will surely awaken bandit hearts.

units.zh: 太常臣謨，平簡貞正，素望所歸，謂可以為都督、徐州刺史。
units.en: He recommended Cai Mo for Xuzhou.
units.literal: Minister Cai Mo is level, simple, upright, and true—the plain expectation returns to him—I say he may serve as Area Commander and Inspector of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 臣亡兄息晉陵內史邁，謙愛養士，甚為流亡所宗，又是臣門戶子弟，堪任兗州刺史。
units.en: He nominated his nephew Xi Mai for Yanzhou.
units.literal: Your servant's late elder brother's son, Administrator of Jinling Mai, humble and cherishing officers, is greatly looked to by exiles; moreover he is a youth of your servant's gate and lineage—fit to be Inspector of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 公家之事，知無不為，是以敢希祁奚之舉。」
units.en: Like Qi Xi he recommended kin on merit."
units.literal: In public-house affairs knowing there is nothing not to be done—therefore dare hope for the deed of Qi Xi.

units.zh: 疏奏，以蔡謨為鑒軍司。
units.en: The court named Cai Mo Xi Jian's army chief of staff.
units.literal: When the memorial was presented, Cai Mo was made Jian's army liaison.

units.zh: 鑒尋薨，時年七十一。
units.en: Xi Jian died at seventy-one.
units.literal: Jian soon died, aged seventy-one.

units.zh: 帝朝晡哭于朝堂，遣御史持節護喪事，贈一依溫嶠故事。
units.en: The emperor mourned at court and funded the funeral like Wen Jiao's.
units.literal: The emperor wept at court in the afternoon; sent a censor bearing credential to oversee funeral affairs; gifts followed Wen Jiao's precedent.

units.zh: 冊曰：「惟公道德沖邃，體識弘遠，忠亮雅正，行為世表，歷位內外，勳庸彌著。
units.en: The edict praised his moral depth, faithful service, and shining merit at home and abroad: "
units.literal: The patent read: "Only my lord's virtue deep and remote, substance and insight vast and far, loyal and bright, correct and elegant, conduct is generation's model—offices within and without, merit ever shining.

units.zh: 乃者約峻狂狡，毒流朝廷，社稷之危，賴公以寧。
units.en: He had saved the throne from Zu Yue and Su Jun.
units.literal: Then Yue and Jun were violent and cunning; poison spread through court—danger to altars and grain relied on my lord to be pacified.

units.zh: 功侔古烈，勳邁桓文。
units.en: His deeds rivaled the ancient worthies and outshone Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
units.literal: Merit matches ancient fierceness; achievement surpasses Huan and Wen.

units.zh: 方倚大猷，藩翼時難，昊天不弔，奄忽薨殂，朕用震悼于厥心。
units.en: The emperor relied on him—Heaven took him instead.
units.literal: Just relying on your great plan to wing the age through hardship—August Heaven shows no pity—suddenly you died; We use trembling grief in Our heart.

units.zh: 夫爵以顯德，諡以表行，所以崇明軌迹，丕揚徽劭。
units.en: Titles honor virtue and conduct.
units.literal: Rank is to display virtue; posthumous title is to manifest conduct—thereby clarifying bright tracks and greatly raising glorious merit.

units.zh: 今贈太宰，諡曰文成，祠以太牢。
units.en: They posthumously named him grand tutor with cult title Cultured Accomplished.
units.literal: Now posthumously award Grand Tutor, posthumous title Cultured Accomplished, sacrifice with grand ox, sheep, and pig.

units.zh: 魂而有靈，嘉茲寵榮。」
units.en: May his spirit relish this honor."
units.literal: If soul has awareness, rejoice in this favor and glory.

units.zh: 初，鑒值永嘉喪亂，在鄉里甚窮餒，鄉人以鑒名德，傳共飴之。
units.en: During the Yongjia chaos Xi Jian starved until neighbors fed him for his reputation.
units.literal: At first when Jian encountered Yongjia's turmoil he was extremely poor and starving in his village; villagers because of Jian's name and virtue passed food together to feed him.

units.zh: 時兄子邁、外甥周翼並小，常攜之就食。
units.en: He carried little Xi Mai and Zhou Yi to every meal.
units.literal: At the time his elder brother's son Mai and sister's son Zhou Yi were still small; he often carried them to go eat.

units.zh: 鄉人曰：「各自饑困，以君賢，欲共相濟耳，恐不能兼有所存。」
units.en: Neighbors said, "We are each starving ourselves; because you are worthy we wish to aid one another—we fear we cannot preserve both."
units.literal: Villagers said: "Each himself hungry and distressed—because you are worthy we wish jointly to aid you—afraid we cannot jointly preserve both."

units.zh: 鑒於是獨往，食訖，以飯著兩頰邊，還吐與二兒，後並得存，同過江。
units.en: Xi Jian went alone, tucked rice in his cheeks, and fed the boys back home—both lived to cross the south.
units.literal: Jian thereupon went alone; when finished eating he put rice at both cheek sides, returned and spat it for the two children; afterward both survived and together crossed the Yangzi.

units.zh: 邁位至護軍，翼為剡縣令。
units.en: Xi Mai became guards commander; Zhou Yi magistrate of Shan.
units.literal: Mai rose to Guards commander; Yi became magistrate of Shan county.

units.zh: 鑒之薨也，翼追撫育之恩，解職而歸，席苫心喪三年。
units.en: At Xi Jian's death Zhou Yi quit office, mourned on straw matting three years for raising him.
units.literal: When Jian died, Yi remembering nurture grace resigned office and returned, spreading straw and observing heart-mourning three years.

units.zh: 二子：愔、曇。
units.en: His sons were Xi Yin and Xi Tan.
units.literal: Two sons: Yin and Tan.

units.zh: 子愔
units.en: Section: Xi Yin.
units.literal: The son Yin.

units.zh: =愔字方回。
units.en: Xi Yin, courtesy name Fanghui.
units.literal: =Yin courtesy name Fanghui.

units.zh: 少不交競，弱冠，除散騎侍郎，不拜。
units.en: He eschewed rivalry; at twenty he was offered attendant gentleman but declined.
units.literal: In youth he did not contend for precedence; at the capping age he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at Yellow Gates—did not accept.

units.zh: 性至孝，居父母憂，殆將滅性。
units.en: He mourned his parents until his health nearly failed.
units.literal: His nature was utmost filial; dwelling in mourning for parents he nearly extinguished his nature.

units.zh: 服闋，襲爵南昌公，徵拜中書侍郎。
units.en: After mourning he inherited the Nanchang dukedom and accepted a secretariat post.
units.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the Duke of Nanchang rank and was summoned Gentleman of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 驃騎何充輔政，征北將軍褚裒鎮京口，皆以愔為長史。
units.en: He Chong and Chu Pou both employed him as chief administrator.
units.literal: When General of Agile Cavalry He Chong assisted governance and General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou held Jingkou, both took Yin as senior clerk.

units.zh: 再遷黃門侍郎。
units.en: He rose twice to attendant gentleman at the gates.
units.literal: He was twice transferred Gentleman at Yellow Gates.

units.zh: 時吳郡守闋，欲以愔為太守。
units.en: Wu commandery wanted him as governor.
units.literal: At the time Wu commandery lacked an administrator; they wished Yin for governor.

units.zh: 愔自以資望少，不宜超蒞大郡，朝議嘉之。
units.en: He judged himself too junior for so large a post—the court admired his modesty.
units.literal: Yin himself thought his seniority and prestige slight—not fitting to leap to a great commandery—court deliberation praised this.

units.zh: 轉為臨海太守。
units.en: They named him instead magistrate of Linhai.
units.literal: He was transferred Administrator of Linhai.

units.zh: 會弟曇卒，益無處世意，在郡優遊，頗稱簡默，與姊夫王羲之、高士許詢並有邁世之風，俱棲心絕谷，修黃老之術。
units.en: After Xi Tan died he coasted through Linhai with Wang Xizhi and Xu Xun, practicing Daoist quietism.
units.literal: When his younger brother Tan died he grew still less inclined toward worldly office; in the commandery he wandered at leisure, quite called terse and silent—together with brother-in-law Wang Xizhi and recluse Xu Xun he had transcendent air; all lodged hearts in hidden valleys, cultivating Huang-Lao arts.

units.zh: 後以疾去職，乃築宅章安，有終焉之志。
units.en: Illness drove him to retire and build a villa at Zhang'an to die in peace.
units.literal: Later because of illness he left office; then built a house in Zhang'an with intent to end life there.

units.zh: 十許年間，人事頓絕。
units.en: For a decade he cut ties with the world.
units.literal: Within ten-odd years human affairs abruptly ceased.

units.zh: 簡文帝輔政，與尚書僕射江虨等薦愔，以為執德存正，識懷沈敏，而辭職遺榮，有不拔之操，成務須才，豈得遂其獨善，宜見徵引，以參政術。
units.en: Emperor Jianwen and Jiang Bin urged him back: virtue, depth, integrity—and the realm needed him.
units.literal: When Emperor Jianwen assisted governance, together with Executive Assistant Jiang Bin and others they recommended Yin, holding he grasped virtue and preserved rectitude, insight deep and keen, yet resigned office leaving glory—having unshakeable integrity—accomplishing tasks needs talent—how can one indulge solitary goodness—fitting to summon and draw in to join governance arts.

units.zh: 於是徵為光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
units.en: They recalled him as grand master of splendid happiness with attendant cavalry.
units.literal: Thereupon he was summoned Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, additionally Attendant Cavalry Regular.

units.zh: 既到，更除太常，固讓不拜。
units.en: They tried to make him minister of ceremonies; he refused.
units.literal: Having arrived, again appointed Minister of Ceremonies—firmly declined and did not accept.

units.zh: 深抱沖退，樂補遠郡，從之，出為輔國將軍、會稽內史。
units.en: He pleaded for a distant post and became supporting-state general and Kuaiji administrator.
units.literal: Deeply embracing humility and withdrawal, happy to fill a distant commandery—they followed it—he went out as General Who Supports the State and Administrator of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 大司馬桓溫以愔與徐兗有故義，乃遷愔都督徐兗青幽揚州之晉陵諸軍事、領徐兗二州刺史、假節。
units.en: Huan Wen, citing old ties to Xu and Yan, reassigned him area commander over five jurisdictions with two provincial inspectorships.
units.literal: Grand Marshal Huan Wen because Yin had old friendship with Xu Yan shifted Yin to Area Commander of Xu Yan Qing You Yangzhou's Jinling military affairs, concurrently Inspector of Xu and Yan two provinces, acting credential.

units.zh: 雖居藩鎮，非其好也。
units.en: Frontier command never suited him.
units.literal: Although dwelling in a screen command, it was not his liking.

units.zh: 俄屬桓溫北伐，愔請督所部出河上，用其子超計，以己非將帥才，不堪軍旅，又固辭解職，勸溫並領己所統。
units.en: When Huan Wen marched north Xi Yin meant to join until Xi Chao urged him to admit he was no soldier—yield command to Huan Wen.
units.literal: Shortly Huan Wen campaigned north; Yin requested to lead his division onto the river north; using his son Chao's plan—because he himself lacked commander's talent and could not bear armies—again firmly declined office and urged Wen to absorb his troops.

units.zh: 轉冠軍將軍、會稽內史。
units.en: He became champion general and Kuaiji administrator again.
units.literal: Transferred Champion General and Administrator of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 及帝踐阼，就加鎮軍、都督浙江東五郡軍事。
units.en: The new emperor added general who guards the army and five eastern Zhejiang commands.
units.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne he was additionally invested General Who Guards the Army and Area Commander of five Zhejiang-east commanderies.

units.zh: 久之，以年老乞骸骨，因居會稽。
units.en: Age drove him to retire in Kuaiji.
units.literal: After long time, because of old age begged bones; therefore dwelt in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 徵拜司空，詔書優美，敦獎殷勤，固辭不起。
units.en: They summoned him as minister of works with glowing edicts—he stayed put.
units.literal: Summoned Minister of Works—edict language generous and beautiful, urging reward earnest—firmly declined and did not rise.

units.zh: 太元九年卒，時年七十二。
units.en: In the ninth year of Taiyuan, he died at seventy-two.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Taiyuan, he died, aged seventy-two.

units.zh: 追贈侍中、司空，諡曰文穆。
units.en: Posthumous honors: palace attendant, minister of works, cult title Cultured Mild.
units.literal: Posthumously awarded Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; posthumous title Cultured Mild.

units.zh: 三子。
units.en: He had three sons.
units.literal: Three sons.

units.zh: 超、融、沖。
units.en: Xi Chao, Xi Rong, Xi Chong.
units.literal: Chao, Rong, Chong.

units.zh: 超最知名。
units.en: Xi Chao became the famous one.
units.literal: Chao was most renowned.

units.zh: 愔子超
units.en: Section: Xi Chao.
units.literal: Yin's son Chao.

units.zh: =超字景興，一字嘉賓。
units.en: Xi Chao, courtesy name Jingxing, also known as Jiabin.
units.literal: =Chao courtesy name Jingxing, alternate name Jiabin.

units.zh: 少卓犖不羈，有曠世之度，交遊士林，每存勝拔，善談論，義理精微。
units.en: Young Xi Chao was brilliant, generous, and razor-sharp in debate.
units.literal: In youth outstanding and unbridled, having breadth transcending the age; associating with scholar gentlemen he constantly wished to lift the eminent; skilled in discourse, meaning subtle and refined.

units.zh: 愔事天師道，而超奉佛。
units.en: Xi Yin followed Celestial Master Daoism; Xi Chao embraced Buddhism.
units.literal: Yin served the Celestial Master Dao; Chao honored Buddhism.

units.zh: 愔又好聚斂，積錢數千萬，嘗開庫，任超所取。
units.en: His father hoarded millions yet opened the treasury to him.
units.literal: Yin also loved gathering wealth—accumulated cash tens of millions—once opened treasury letting Chao take freely.

units.zh: 超性好施，一日中散與親故都盡。
units.en: Xi Chao gave every coin away in a single day.
units.literal: Chao by nature loved giving—in one day scattered all to kin and old friends.

units.zh: 其任心獨詣，皆此類也。
units.en: He lived by impulse alone.
units.literal: His following heart unique penetration—all was of this kind.

units.zh: 桓溫辟為征西大將軍掾。
units.en: Huan Wen took him as staff to the western expedition.
units.literal: Huan Wen summoned him as aide to General Who Conquers the West.

units.zh: 溫遷大司馬，又轉為參軍。
units.en: When Huan Wen became grand marshal Xi Chao followed as aide.
units.literal: When Wen shifted Grand Marshal he again transferred to aide.

units.zh: 溫英氣高邁，罕有所推，與超言，常謂不能測，遂傾意禮待。
units.en: Proud Huan Wen deferred to almost no one yet admitted Xi Chao outthought him.
units.literal: Wen's heroic spirit towered—rarely deferring to anyone—with Chao in discourse often said he could not fathom him; thereupon poured intent courteous treatment.

units.zh: 超亦深自結納。
units.en: Xi Chao returned the devotion.
units.literal: Chao also deeply attached himself.

units.zh: 時王珣為溫主簿，亦為溫所重。
units.en: Wang Xun served as chief clerk—another favorite.
units.literal: At the time Wang Xun was Wen's chief clerk—also weighted by Wen.

units.zh: 府中語曰：「髯參軍，短主簿，能令公喜，能令公怒。」
units.en: The headquarters rhyme ran: "The bearded aide, the short chief clerk—delight him or enrage him."
units.literal: Headquarters rhyme said: "Bearded aide, short chief clerk—can make the lord joyful, can make the lord angry.

units.zh: 超髯，珣短故也。
units.en: Xi Chao wore a beard; Wang Xun was short.
units.literal: —because Chao was bearded and Xun short.

units.zh: 尋除散騎侍郎。
units.en: He became attendant gentleman at the gates.
units.literal: Shortly appointed Gentleman Attendant at Yellow Gates.

units.zh: 時愔在北府，徐州人多勁悍，溫恆云「京口酒可飲，兵可用」，深不欲愔居之。
units.en: Xi Yin was at Northern Headquarters; Xuzhou men were fierce and hardy. Huan Wen constantly said, "Jingkou's wine is drinkable and its troops usable"—he deeply did not wish Yin to hold that post.
units.literal: At the time Yin was at Northern Headquarters—Xuzhou men mostly fierce and hardy—Wen constantly said "Jingkou wine may be drunk, troops may be used"—deeply did not wish Yin to dwell there.

units.zh: 而愔暗於事機，遣箋詣溫，欲共獎王室，修復園陵。
units.en: Xi Yin naïvely wrote offering joint service to restore the tombs.
units.literal: Yet Yin was dim on affairs' pivot; sent a note to Wen wishing jointly to aid the royal house and restore the imperial tombs.

units.zh: 超取視，寸寸毀裂，乃更作箋，自陳老病，甚不堪人間，乞閑地自養。
units.en: Xi Chao shredded it and drafted a plea ill-health and need for quiet retirement.
units.literal: Chao took it to read and tore it inch by inch; then composed another note stating old illness—quite unable to bear human realm—begging idle lands to nurture himself.

units.zh: 溫得箋大喜，即轉愔為會稽太守。
units.en: Delighted, Huan Wen moved Xi Yin to Kuaiji.
units.literal: Wen receiving the note greatly rejoiced—thereupon shifted Yin to Administrator of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 溫懷不軌，欲立霸王之基，超為之謀。
units.en: Xi Chao plotted Huan Wen's bid for hegemony.
units.literal: Wen harbored designs beyond duty—wishing to lay overlord foundation—Chao schemed for him.

units.zh: 謝安與王坦之嘗詣溫論事，溫令超帳中臥聽之，風動帳開，安笑曰：「郗生可謂入幕之賓矣。」
units.en: Xie An found Xi Chao eavesdropping from Huan Wen's tent—the classic "guest behind the curtain."
units.literal: Xie An and Wang Tanzhi once visited Wen to discuss affairs; Wen ordered Chao to lie in the tent listening—wind moved the curtain open—An smiled saying: "Master Xi may be called guest who entered the curtain."

units.zh: 太和中，溫將伐慕容氏於臨漳，超諫以道遠，汴水又淺，運道不通。
units.en: During Taihe, Huan Wen targeted Yecheng; Xi Chao cited distance and shallow rivers blocking supply.
units.literal: In Taihe era Wen was about to campaign against the Murong clan at Linzhang—Chao remonstrated that the road was far, Bian River also shallow—transport route impassable.

units.zh: 溫不從，遂引軍自濟入河，超又進策于溫曰：「清水入河，無通運理。
units.en: Huan Wen marched from the Ji into the Yellow River anyway; Xi Chao warned, "Clear streams feeding the river cannot float supplies.
units.literal: Wen did not follow; thereupon led army from Ji into the river—Chao again advanced stratagem to Wen saying: "Clear water entering the river—no principle of open transport.

units.zh: 若寇不戰，運道又難，因資無所，實為深慮也。
units.en: If they refuse battle and supply lines stall, you have nothing to feed on—that is the danger.
units.literal: If the enemy does not give battle and transport is again difficult—with nowhere to draw supplies—this is truly deep worry.

units.zh: 今盛夏，悉力徑造鄴城，彼伏公威略，必望陣而走，退還幽朔矣。
units.en: Strike Yecheng this summer while morale holds—they will bolt north at your name.
units.literal: Now in blazing summer strike straight for Yecheng with full force—they will yield to your lord's martial prestige and surely flee at sight of the line, retreating to You and Shuo.

units.zh: 若能決戰，呼吸可定。
units.en: Force a pitched battle and it ends in an afternoon.
units.literal: If they can be forced to decisive battle, in a breath it may be settled.

units.zh: 設欲城鄴，難為功力。
units.en: A prolonged siege exhausts the army.
units.literal: Suppose you wish to besiege Yecheng—the labor of siege works is hard.

units.zh: 百姓布野，盡為官有。
units.en: The countryside yields supplies for your camp.
units.literal: Common people spread across the wilds—all become officials' possession.

units.zh: 易水以南，必交臂請命。
units.en: South of the Yi they will surrender in strings.
units.literal: South of the Yi River they will surely fold arms and beg terms.

units.zh: 但恐此計輕決，公必務其持重耳。
units.en: Only mind rash orders—you prize steadiness.
units.literal: Only I fear this plan lightly decided—my lord surely strives for cautious weight.

units.zh: 若此計不從，便當頓兵河濟，控引糧運，令資儲充備，足及來夏，雖如賒遲，終亦濟克。
units.en: Or halt between the Ji and Yellow Rivers, stockpile grain until next summer—slow but sure.
units.literal: If this plan is not followed then halt troops between Yellow and Ji, control grain transport, cause provisions fully prepared—sufficient until next summer—though seemingly delayed, in the end success can be achieved.

units.zh: 若舍此二策而連軍西進，進不速決，退必愆乏，賊因此勢，日月相引，僶俛秋冬，船道澀滯，且北土早寒，三軍裘褐者少，恐不可以涉冬。
units.en: March west instead and stall—retreat starves you; seasons turn; autumn floods ice northern rivers; troops lack winter coats—you may not survive the cold.
units.literal: If abandoning these two strategies and linking armies westward—advance not swift in decision, retreat surely deficient in supplies—the bandits riding this momentum, sun and moon pulling each other along, struggling through autumn and winter—water routes sluggish—and moreover northern soil early cold—the three armies few in fur coats—I fear they cannot cross winter.

units.zh: 此大限閡，非惟無食而已。」
units.en: That is annihilation—not mere hunger."
units.literal: This is the great barrier—not merely lacking food.

units.zh: 溫不從，果有枋頭之敗，溫深慚之。
units.en: Huan Wen ignored him and lost at Fangtou—humiliation followed.
units.literal: Wen did not follow—indeed there was defeat at Fangtou—Wen deeply shamed himself.

units.zh: 尋而有壽陽之捷，問超曰：「此足以雪枋頭之恥乎？」
units.en: After Shouyang he asked, "Does this erase Fangtou?"
units.literal: Shortly there was victory at Shouyang; he asked Chao: "Does this suffice to wash away Fangtou's shame?

units.zh: 超曰：「未厭有識之情也。」
units.en: Xi Chao said, "Thoughtful men remain unsatisfied."
units.literal: Chao said: "It does not satisfy minds of insight.

units.zh: 既而超就溫宿，中夜謂溫曰：「明公都有慮不？」
units.en: That night he whispered, "Are you still uneasy?"
units.literal: Later Chao lodged with Wen; midnight he said to Wen: "My lord altogether has worries or not?

units.zh: 溫曰：「卿欲有所言邪？」
units.en: Huan Wen asked, "What is it?"
units.literal: Wen said: "Do you wish to speak something?

units.zh: 超曰：「明公既居重任，天下之責將歸於公矣。
units.en: Xi Chao said, "You hold peak power—the world blames you.
units.literal: Chao said: "My lord already bears heavy responsibility—the realm's blame will return to my lord.

units.zh: 若不能行廢立大事、為伊霍之舉者，不足鎮壓四海，震服宇內，豈可不深思哉！」
units.en: Without an Yi Yin coup you cannot awe the empire—think hard."
units.literal: If you cannot carry out the great deed of deposition and enthronement—the deed of Yi Yin and Huo Guang—not enough to suppress within the four seas and awe within the realm—how can you not ponder deeply!

units.zh: 溫既素有此計，深納其言，遂定廢立，超始謀也。
units.en: Huan Wen already wanted depositions—Xi Chao sealed it—the verdict was his idea.
units.literal: Wen since long had harbored this plan—deeply absorbed his words—thereupon settled deposition and enthronement—Chao began the plot.

units.zh: 遷中書侍郎。
units.en: He rose to secretariat gentleman.
units.literal: Promoted Gentleman of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 謝安嘗與王文度共詣超，日旰未得前，文度便欲去，安曰：「不能為性命忍俄頃邪！」
units.en: Xie An waited all day to see Xi Chao—Wang Tanzhi lost patience; Xie snapped, "Cannot endure a moment for your career?"
units.literal: Xie An once together with Wang Tanzhi visited Chao—sunset came yet could not advance—Tanzhi wished to leave—An said: "Cannot for life's sake endure a moment!

units.zh: 其權重當時如此。
units.en: Such was Xi Chao's pull.
units.literal: His weight of power was thus at the time.

units.zh: 轉司徒左長史，母喪去職。
units.en: He became chief clerk under the minister of education until mourning dismissed him.
units.literal: Transferred Senior Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Education—mother's mourning removed office.

units.zh: 常謂其父名公之子，位遇應在謝安右，而安入掌機權，愔優遊而已，恆懷憤憤，發言慷慨，由是與謝氏不穆。
units.en: He thought Xi Yin deserved higher rank than Xie An—resented Xie's power—and feuded with the Xies.
units.literal: He constantly held that his father was son of a famed lord—rank and fortune ought to stand right of Xie An—yet An entered grasping secret authority while Yin wandered idly—always harboring resentment—speech forthright and stirring—thereby with Xie clan not harmonious.

units.zh: 安亦深恨之。
units.en: Xie An hated him back.
units.literal: An also deeply hated him.

units.zh: 服闋，除散騎常侍，不起。
units.en: After mourning they offered attendant cavalry—he stayed home.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Attendant Cavalry Regular—did not rise.

units.zh: 以為臨海太守，加宣威將軍，不拜。
units.en: They named him Linhai governor with generalship—he refused.
units.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Linhai, additionally General Who Spreads Might—did not accept.

units.zh: 年四十二，先愔卒。
units.en: He died at forty-two, predeceasing his father.
units.literal: Age forty-two—died before Yin.

units.zh: 初，超雖實黨桓氏，以愔忠於王室，不令知之。
units.en: Though Xi Chao backed Huan Wen he hid it from his loyal father.
units.literal: At first although Chao truly sided with the Huan clan—because Yin was loyal to the royal house—he did not let him know.

units.zh: 將亡，出一箱書，付門生曰：「本欲焚之，恐公年尊，必以傷愍為弊。
units.en: Dying, he gave a sealed chest to a student: "I had meant to burn it, fearing that at your advanced age grief would harm you.
units.literal: About to die he brought out a chest of documents, handed to a disciple saying: "Originally wished to burn them—afraid my lord is aged—surely would take wounded pity as harm.

units.zh: 我亡後，若大損眠食，可呈此箱。
units.en: If mourning destroys his health, show him the chest.
units.literal: After I die if greatly harmed in sleep and food—may present this chest.

units.zh: 不爾，便燒之。」
units.en: Otherwise burn it."
units.literal: If not—then burn them.

units.zh: 愔後果哀悼成疾，門生依旨呈之，則悉與溫往反密計。
units.en: Xi Yin fell ill with grief; the chest revealed Xi Chao's letters to Huan Wen.
units.literal: Yin afterward indeed mourned into illness—the disciple according to instruction presented them—then wholly secret plans exchanged with Wen.

units.zh: 愔於是大怒曰：「小子死恨晚矣！」
units.en: Xi Yin roared, "He should have died sooner!"
units.literal: Yin thereupon greatly raged saying: "The boy—death hatred comes late!

units.zh: 更不復哭。
units.en: He never wept for Xi Chao again.
units.literal: No longer wept.

units.zh: 凡超所交友，皆一時秀美，雖寒門後進，亦拔而友之。
units.en: Xi Chao befriended talent great and small alike.
units.literal: All whom Chao befriended were moment's finest—even humble-house later entrants—he raised and befriended them.

units.zh: 及死之日，貴賤操筆而為誄者四十餘人，其為眾所宗貴如此。
units.en: Forty scholars wrote his elegy—such was his stature.
units.literal: At day of death noble and base took brush composing elegies—over forty persons—thus was he honored by the multitude.

units.zh: 王獻之兄弟，自超未亡，見愔，常躡履問訊，甚修舅甥之禮。
units.en: The Wang brothers tiptoed to honor Xi Yin while Xi Chao lived.
units.literal: Wang Xianzhi and brothers—before Chao had not died—seeing Yin—always tiptoed in slippers inquiring after health—greatly observing uncle-nephew courtesy.

units.zh: 及超死，見愔慢怠，屐而候之，命席便遷延辭避。
units.en: After Xi Chao died they loitered in clogs and snubbed him.
units.literal: When Chao died—seeing Yin negligent and slack—shoes on waited on him—ordering seat then drew back declining.

units.zh: 愔每慨然曰：「使嘉賓不死，鼠子敢爾邪！」
units.en: Xi Yin muttered, "If Jiabin lived, those runts would never dare."
units.literal: Yin often sighed saying: "Had Jiabin not died—would ratlings dare thus!

units.zh: 性好聞人棲遁，有能辭榮拂衣者，超為之起屋宇，作器服，畜僕豎，費百金而不吝。
units.en: He bankrolled hermits lavishly—houses, robes, servants—without counting gold.
units.literal: By nature fond of hearing men recluse and flee—those able to resign glory and brush garment—Chao for them raised houses, made vessels and clothes, kept servants—costing hundred in gold yet not stingy.

units.zh: 又沙門支遁以清談著名于時，風流勝貴，莫不崇敬，以為造微之功，足參諸正始。
units.en: Monk Zhi Dun's wit rivaled the Zhengshi sages.
units.literal: Moreover monk Zhi Dun by pure discourse was famed in the age—elegant and noble—none did not revere—holding his subtle achievement sufficient to join Zhengshi masters.

units.zh: 而遁常重超，以為一時之俊，甚相知賞。
units.en: Zhi Dun ranked Xi Chao chief among his generation.
units.literal: Yet Dun constantly esteemed Chao—holding him moment's finest—greatly knowing and appreciating each other.

units.zh: 超無子，從弟儉之以子僧施嗣。
units.en: He adopted his cousin's son Xi Sengshi as heir.
units.literal: Chao had no son—cousin Jianzhi made son Sengshi heir.

units.zh: 僧施字惠脫，襲爵南昌公。
units.en: Xi Sengshi—courtesy Huituo—inherited the Nanchang dukedom.
units.literal: Sengshi courtesy name Huituo—inherited Duke of Nanchang rank.

units.zh: 弱冠，與王綏、桓胤齊名，累居清顯，領宣城內史，入補丹陽尹。
units.en: At twenty he matched Wang Sui and Huan Yin in fame; he governed Xuancheng and became Danyang intendant.
units.literal: At capping age together with Wang Sui and Huan Yin equally famed—successively dwelt in pure and eminent posts—held Administrator of Xuancheng—entered as supplement Governor of Danyang.

units.zh: 劉毅鎮江陵，請為南蠻校尉、假節。
units.en: Liu Yi named him southern tribes colonel at Jiangling.
units.literal: Liu Yi garrisoned Jiangling—requested him as Colonel of Southern Barbarians, acting credential.

units.zh: 與毅俱誅，國除。
units.en: Liu Yi's fall cost him his life and his title.
units.literal: Together with Yi executed—noble house abolished.

units.zh: 愔弟曇
units.en: Section: Xi Tan.
units.literal: Yin's younger brother Tan.

units.zh: =曇字重熙，少賜爵東安縣開國伯。
units.en: Xi Tan, courtesy Chongxi, received the Dong'an barony in youth.
units.literal: =Tan courtesy name Chongxi—in youth enfeoffed Baron Who Founded the Nation of Dong'an.

units.zh: 司徒王導辟秘書郎。
units.en: Wang Dao named him secretary gentleman.
units.literal: Minister of Education Wang Dao summoned him Secretary Gentleman.

units.zh: 朝論以曇名臣之子，每逼以憲制，年三十，始拜通直散騎侍郎，遷中書侍郎。
units.en: Court etiquette delayed his rise until thirty—then attendant gentleman and secretariat posts.
units.literal: Court opinion because Tan was son of a famed minister—each time pressed him with statutory rule—age thirty—only then appointed Attendant Cavalry Regular on straight duty—promoted Secretariat Gentleman.

units.zh: 簡文帝為撫軍，引為司馬。
units.en: Emperor Jianwen made him army major.
units.literal: When Emperor Jianwen was General Who Pacifies the Army—drew him in as Major.

units.zh: 尋除尚書吏部郎，拜御史中丞。
units.en: He rose to personnel director and censor-in-chief.
units.literal: Shortly appointed Personnel Minister of the Ministry of Personnel—invested Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 時北中郎荀羨有疾，朝廷以曇為羨軍司，加散騎常侍。
units.en: When Xun Xian fell ill Xi Tan became his army chief of staff.
units.literal: At the time North Commandant Xun Xian was ill—the court made Tan Xian's army liaison, additionally Attendant Cavalry Regular.

units.zh: 頃之，羨征還，仍除北中郎將、都督徐兗青幽揚州之晉陵諸軍事、領徐兗二州刺史、假節，鎮下邳，後與賊帥傅末波等戰失利，降號建威將軍。
units.en: He succeeded Xun Xian as northern commander at Xiapi, lost to Fu Mobo, and was demoted to general who establishes might.
units.literal: Shortly Xun recalled from campaign—Tan still appointed North Commandant, Area Commander of Xu Yan Qing You Yangzhou's Jinling military affairs, concurrently Inspector of Xu and Yan two provinces, acting credential, garrisoned Xiapi—later fought bandit chief Fu Mobo and others losing—reduced in rank to General Who Establishes Might.

units.zh: 尋卒，年四十二。
units.en: He died at forty-two.
units.literal: Soon died—age forty-two.

units.zh: 追贈北中郎，諡曰簡。
units.en: Posthumous rank north commandant, cult title Simple.
units.literal: Posthumously awarded North Commandant—posthumous title Simple.

units.zh: 子恢嗣。
units.en: His son Xi Hui inherited.
units.literal: Son Hui succeeded.

units.zh: 恢字道胤，少襲父爵，散騎侍郎，累遷給事黃門侍郎，領太子右衛率。
units.en: Xi Hui inherited young, rose to gentleman attendant and right guard of the heir.
units.literal: Hui courtesy name Daoyin—in youth inherited father's noble rank—Gentleman Attendant at Yellow Gates—rose to Gentleman for Submission at Yellow Gates—concurrently Junior General Guarding the Heir's Right.

units.zh: 恢身長八尺，美鬢髯，孝武帝深器之，以為有藩伯之望。
units.en: Eight chi tall with a splendid beard, Emperor Xiaowu marked him for frontier command.
units.literal: Hui's body eight chi tall—beautiful beard—Emperor Xiaowu deeply esteemed him—holding he had prospect of screen lord.

units.zh: 會硃序自表去職，擢恢為梁秦雍司荊揚並等州諸軍事、建威將軍、雍州刺史、假節，鎮襄陽。
units.en: When Zhu Xu stepped down Xi Hui took Yongzhou and supreme command at Xiangyang.
units.literal: When Zhu Xu memorialized leaving office—promoted Hui Area Commander of Liang Qin Yong Si Jing Yang Bing and other states' military affairs—General Who Establishes Might—Inspector of Yongzhou—acting credential—garrisoned Xiangyang.

units.zh: 恢甚得關隴之和，降附者動有千計。
units.en: He pacified Guanlong; thousands flocked to him.
units.literal: Hui very obtained harmony of Guan and Long—those surrendering attached numbered often in thousands.

units.zh: 初，姚萇將竇沖來降，拜東羌校尉。
units.en: Dou Chong defected from Yao Chang and became eastern Qiang colonel.
units.literal: At first Yao Chang's officer Dou Chong came to surrender—invested Colonel of Eastern Qiang.

units.zh: 沖後舉兵反，入漢川，襲梁州。
units.en: Dou Chong rebelled into Hanzhong and struck Liangzhou.
units.literal: Chong later raised troops rebelling—entered Hanzhong—raided Liangzhou.

units.zh: 時關中有巴蜀之眾，皆背萇，據弘農以結苻登。
units.en: Ba-Shu troops in Guanzhong turned on Yao Chang and backed Fu Deng at Hongnong.
units.literal: At the time within Guanzhong were Ba-Shu hosts—all betrayed Chang—occupying Hongnong to ally Fu Deng.

units.zh: 而登署沖為左丞相，徙屯華陰。
units.en: Fu Deng named Dou Chong left chancellor at Huayin.
units.literal: And Deng appointed Chong Left Chancellor—shifted encampment to Huayin.

units.zh: 河南太守楊佺期遣上党太守荀靜戍皇天塢以距之。
units.en: Yang Quanqi posted Xun Jing at Huangtianwu against Dou Chong.
units.literal: Administrator of Henan Yang Quanqi sent Administrator of Shangdang Xun Jing garrison Huangtian Ridge to block him.

units.zh: 沖數來攻，恢遣將軍趙睦守金墉城，而佺期率眾次湖城，討沖，走之。
units.en: Dou Chong stormed the line; Xi Hui held Jinyong while Yang Quanqi drove him back from Hucheng.
units.literal: Chong repeatedly came attacking—Hui sent General Zhao Mu guard Jinyong City—while Quanqi led hosts halted at Hucheng—punishing Chong—routing him.

units.zh: 尋而慕容垂圍慕容永於潞川，永窮蹙，遣其子弘求救於恢，並獻玉璽一紐，恢獻璽於台，又陳「垂若並永，其勢難測。
units.en: Murong Chui besieged Murong Yong at Lu River; Yong sent his son Hong with the imperial seal seeking Jin aid—Xi Hui warned that "if Chui swallows Yong, their momentum will be hard to gauge.
units.literal: Shortly Murong Chui besieged Murong Yong at Lu River—Yong pressed tight—sent son Hong begging rescue from Hui—and presented one jade seal knob—Hui presented seal to court—also stating "If Chui swallows Yong—their momentum hard to measure.

units.zh: 今于國計，謂宜救永。
units.en: For the realm's interest Jin should aid Yong.
units.literal: Now for state plan—I say fitting to rescue Yong.

units.zh: 永垂並存，自為仇讎，連雞不棲，無能為患。
units.en: Let both Murongs bleed each other—they cannot cooperate.
units.literal: Yong and Chui together existing—naturally become mutual foes—chained chickens do not roost—unable to become trouble.

units.zh: 然後乘機雙斃，則河北可平」。
units.en: Then strike both opportunely and Hebei may be pacified."
units.literal: Then riding opportunity slaying both—then Hebei may be pacified.

units.zh: 孝武帝以為然，詔王恭、庾楷救之，未及發而永沒。
units.en: Xiaowu agreed—but Wang Gong never marched before Yong fell.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu held it right—issued an edict Wang Gong and Yu Kai to rescue—before setting out Yong perished.

units.zh: 楊佺期以疾去職。
units.en: Yang Quanqi resigned ill.
units.literal: Yang Quanqi because of illness left office.

units.zh: 恢以隨郡太守夏侯宗之為河南太守，戍洛陽。
units.en: Xi Hui put Xiahou Zongzhi in charge of Luoyang.
units.literal: Hui made Suizhou Administrator Xia Hou Zongzhi Administrator of Henan—garrisoned Luoyang.

units.zh: 姚萇遣其子略攻湖城及上洛，又使其將楊佛嵩圍洛陽。
units.en: Yao Chang struck Hucheng and besieged Luoyang.
units.literal: Yao Chang sent son Lue attack Hucheng and Shangluo—also sent officer Yang Fosong besiege Luoyang.

units.zh: 恢遣建武將軍辛恭靖救洛陽，梁州刺史王正胤率眾出子午穀，以為聲援。
units.en: Xi Hui sent Xin Gongjing to Luoyang and Wang Zhengyin through Ziwu as diversion.
units.literal: Hui sent General Who Establishes Martial Xin Gongjing rescue Luoyang—Liangzhou Inspector Wang Zhengyin led hosts out Ziwu Valley as sounding support.

units.zh: 略懼而退。
units.en: Yao Lue retreated.
units.literal: Lue feared and withdrew.

units.zh: 恢以功進征虜將軍，又領秦州刺史，加督隴上軍。
units.en: Xi Hui earned promotion to general who conquers captives and added Qinzhou.
units.literal: Hui by merit promoted General Who Conquers Captives—also concurrently Inspector of Qinzhou—additionally commanded Longshang armies.

units.zh: 時魏氏強盛，山陵危逼，恢遣江夏相鄧啟方等以萬人距之，與魏主拓跋珪戰于滎陽，大敗而還。
units.en: Tuoba Gui crushed his ten thousand men at Xingyang—near Luoyang's tombs.
units.literal: At the time Wei was strong—imperial tombs imperiled—Hui sent Jiangxia Administrator Deng Qifang and others with ten thousand men oppose them—battled Wei lord Tuoba Gui at Xingyang—greatly defeated returned.

units.zh: 及王恭計王國寶，桓玄、殷仲堪皆舉兵應恭，恢與朝廷掎角玄等。
units.en: Wang Gong's coup drew Huan Xuan and Yin Zhongkan; Xi Hui pinned them from Xiangyang.
units.literal: When Wang Gong plotted Wang Guobao—Huan Xuan and Yin Zhongkan all raised troops aiding Gong—Hui with court cornered Xuan and others.

units.zh: 襄陽太守夏侯宗之、府司馬郭毗並以為不可，恢皆殺之。
units.en: His aides Xiahou Zongzhi and Guo Pi objected—he executed both.
units.literal: Xiangyang Administrator Xia Hou Zongzhi and headquarters aide Guo Pi both held could not—Hui both killed them.

units.zh: 既而玄等退守尋陽。
units.en: The rebels fell back to Xunyang.
units.literal: Shortly Xuan and others retreated guarding Xunyang.

units.zh: 以恢為尚書，將家還都，至楊口，仲堪陰使人於道殺之，及其四子，托以群蠻所殺。
units.en: Recalled as minister of works, Yin Zhongkan ambushed him at Yangkou—murdered him and four sons—blamed tribesmen.
units.literal: Appointed Hui Minister of Works—leading family returning capital—reaching Yangkou—Zhongkan secretly sent men on road killing him—and his four sons—pretending killed by southern barbarians.

units.zh: 喪還京師，贈鎮軍將軍。
units.en: His body reached the capital with posthumous general who guards the army.
units.literal: Coffin returned capital—posthumously awarded General Who Guards the Army.

units.zh: 子循嗣。
units.en: Xi Xun inherited.
units.literal: Son Xun succeeded.

units.zh: 叔父隆
units.en: Section: Xi Long.
units.literal: Paternal uncle Long.

units.zh: =隆字弘始，蹇亮有匪躬之節。
units.en: Xi Long—courtesy Hongshi—was bluntly loyal to the throne.
units.literal: =Long courtesy name Hongshi—upright and bright—having integrity of not sparing self.

units.zh: 初為尚書郎，轉左丞，在朝為百僚所憚，坐漏泄事免。
units.en: He rose in the secretariat, terrified colleagues, and fell for leaking secrets.
units.literal: At first Secretary Gentleman—transferred Left Assistant—in court feared by hundred officials—sat for leaking affairs dismissed.

units.zh: 頃之，為吏部郎，復免。
units.en: Personnel ministry dismissed him again.
units.literal: Shortly Personnel Minister—again dismissed.

units.zh: 補東郡太守。
units.en: They named him Dongjun administrator.
units.literal: Supplemented Administrator of Dongjun.

units.zh: 隆少為趙王倫所善，及倫專擅，召為散騎常侍。
units.en: Prince Zhao Lun favored him and named him attendant cavalry.
units.literal: Long in youth favored by Prince Zhao Lun—and when Lun monopolized power—summoned Attendant Cavalry Regular.

units.zh: 倫之篡也，以為揚州刺史。
units.en: Sima Lun made him Yangzhou inspector.
units.literal: At Lun's usurpation—appointed Inspector of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 僚屬有犯，輒依台閣峻制繩之，遠近咸怨。
units.en: He policed staff harshly—everyone resented him.
units.literal: When subordinates offended—always applied terrace severe statutes binding them—far and near alike resented.

units.zh: 尋加甯東將軍，未拜，而齊王冏檄至，中州人在軍者皆欲赴義，隆以兄子鑒為趙王掾，諸子悉在京洛，故猶豫未決。
units.en: Sima Jiong summoned loyal troops; Xi Long hesitated because kin served Sima Lun.
units.literal: Shortly additionally General Who Pacifies the East—not invested—and Prince of Qi Sima Jiong's proclamation arrived—men of Central Plain in army all wished to respond to righteousness—Long because elder brother's son Jian was Zhao prince aide—all sons in capital Luo—therefore hesitated undecided.

units.zh: 主簿趙誘、前秀才虞潭白隆曰：「當今上計，明使君自將精兵徑赴齊王；
units.en: Zhao You and Yu Tan offered three plans: "As the best plan, my lord should personally lead elite troops straight to the Prince of Qi;
units.literal: Chief Clerk Zhao You—former Cultivated Talent Yu Tan informed Long saying: "Upper plan—enlightened envoy lord personally lead crack troops straight proceed Prince of Qi;

units.zh: 中計，明使君可留督攝，速遣猛將率精兵疾赴；
units.en: Next—stay behind but rush crack troops.
units.literal: Middle plan—enlightened envoy lord may remain supervise command—swift dispatch fierce general lead crack troops urgent proceed;

units.zh: 下計，示遣兵將助，而稱背倫。」
units.en: As the worst plan, appear to dispatch generals to aid him while claiming betrayal of Lun."
units.literal: Lower plan—show dispatch troops generals aiding—yet claiming betray Lun.

units.zh: 隆素敬別駕顧彥，密與謀之。
units.en: Xi Long respected aide Gu Yan and conspired in secret.
units.literal: Long since always esteemed aide Gu Yan—secretly plotted with him.

units.zh: 彥曰：「趙誘下計，乃上策也。」
units.en: Gu Yan said Zhao You's "worst" option was actually best.
units.literal: Yan said: "Zhao You's lower plan is indeed the upper strategy.

units.zh: 西曹留承聞彥言，請見，曰：「不審明使君當今何施？」
units.en: Liu Cheng asked for an audience and said, "I do not know what course my lord intends now?"
units.literal: Western Bureau aide Liu Cheng hearing Yan's words requested audience saying: "May not ask enlightened envoy lord nowadays what policy shall apply?

units.zh: 隆曰：「我俱受二帝恩，無所偏助，惟欲守州而已。」
units.en: Xi Long said, "I alike received grace from both emperors and favor neither side—I only wish to hold the province."
units.literal: Long said: "I alike received grace from two emperors—without partial aid—I only wish to guard the province.

units.zh: 承曰：「天下者，世祖皇帝之天下也。
units.en: Liu Cheng said, "The realm belongs to Emperor Wu's succession.
units.literal: Cheng said: "The realm belongs to Emperor Wu's succession.

units.zh: 太上承代已積十年，今上取四海不平，齊王應天順時，成敗之事可見。
units.en: Emperor Hui had ruled a decade; turmoil ruled the land; Prince of Qi held Heaven's mandate—the outcome was plain.
units.literal: Grandfather succeeding substitute already piled ten years—present emperor obtaining realm unpeaceful—Prince of Qi responds Heaven obeying season—success or defeat's matter may be seen.

units.zh: 使君若顧二帝，自可不行，宜急下檄文，速遣精兵猛將。
units.en: Honor both Simas if you must—but issue orders now and rush reinforcements.
units.literal: If envoy lord attends two emperors—of himself may not march—fitting urgently issue proclamation—swiftly dispatch crack troops fierce generals.

units.zh: 若其疑惑，此州豈可得保也！」
units.en: If you hesitate, can this province be preserved!"
units.literal: If you hesitate—can this province be preserved!

units.zh: 隆無所言，而停檄六日。
units.en: Xi Long stalled six days without issuing orders.
units.literal: Long said nothing—and halted proclamation six days.

units.zh: 時甯遠將軍陳留王邃領東海都尉，鎮石頭，隆軍人西赴邃甚眾。
units.en: Prince Sima Sui of Chenliu held Stone City; Xi Long's men streamed west to join him.
units.literal: At the time General Who Pacifies the Distance Prince of Chenliu Sima Sui concurrently held Donghai commandant—garrisoned Stone Fortress—Long's troops westward to join Sui were extremely numerous.

units.zh: 隆遣從事于牛渚禁之，不得止。
units.en: Xi Long tried to block Niuzhu—they could not stem the tide.
units.literal: Long dispatched clerk at Niuzhu to forbid them—they could not stop.

units.zh: 將士憤怒，夜扶邃為主而攻之，隆父子皆死，顧彥亦被害，誣隆聚合遠近，圖為不軌。
units.en: Soldiers installed Sima Sui as leader, killed Xi Long and Gu Yan, then framed them as traitors.
units.literal: Officers and soldiers enraged—night raised Sui as chief and attacked him—Long father and son both died—Gu Yan also suffered harm—slandering Long gathered far and near plotting unorthodox rebellion.

units.zh: 隆之死也，時議莫不痛惜焉。
units.en: Every observer mourned Xi Long.
units.literal: When Long died—court debate none failed to grieve.

units.zh: 【史評】
units.en: Historians' appraisal section heading.
units.literal: 【Historical appraisal】

units.zh: 史臣曰：忠臣本乎孝子，奉上資乎愛親，自家刑國，於期極矣。
units.en: The editors wrote: loyalty springs from filial duty—the household trains the court.
units.literal: The historians say: Loyal ministers root in filial sons—serving above draws from loving kin—from household norms extend to state—thus fulfillment reaches utmost.

units.zh: 太真性履純深，譽流邦族，始則承顏候色，老萊弗之加也；
units.en: Wen Jiao's character ran pure—he honored his mother beyond Laizi's theatrical devotion.
units.literal: Taizhen's nature practiced purity deep—fame flowed clan and kindred—at first then sustaining expression observing bearing—even Laizi added nothing;

units.zh: 既而辭親蹈義，申胥何以尚焉！
units.en: Then he broke from kin for duty—what Shen Xu did was no greater.
units.literal: Afterward resigning kin treading righteousness—even Shen Xu—how could surpass!

units.zh: 封狐萬里，投軀而弗顧；
units.en: Bandits roamed ten thousand li—he threw himself forward without looking back.
units.literal: The giant fox ten thousand li—casting body without glance;

units.zh: 猰窳千群，探穴而忘死。
units.en: Monsters massed in thousands—he charged their dens heedless of death.
units.literal: The ya demon hosts by thousands—probing dens forgetting death.

units.zh: 竟能宣力王室，揚名本朝，負荷受遺，繼之全節。
units.en: He served the Jin throne, forged his name, inherited the regency mandate, and kept faith unto death.
units.literal: Finally able to exert strength through royal house—raising name within court—bearing accepting testament mandate—continuing with integrity entire.

units.zh: 言念主辱，義聲動於天地；
units.en: Thinking of the emperor's humiliation, his cry shook Heaven and earth;
units.literal: Speaking thinking lord's shame—righteous cry stirred Heaven and Earth;

units.zh: 祗赴國屯，信誓明於日月。
units.en: Rushing to rescue the realm, his oath shone like sun and moon;
units.literal: Respecting rushing national peril—good faith oath bright as sun and moon.

units.zh: 枕戈雨泣，若雪分天之仇；
units.en: He slept on arms and wept—burning to avenge heaven-breaking crimes;
units.literal: Pillow spear weeping in rain—as if washing Heaven-splitting vengeance;

units.zh: 皇輿旋軫，卒復夷庚之躅。
units.en: The royal carriage rolled again—the righteous road reopened;
units.literal: Imperial carriage wheels turning—finally restoring tread on righteous highway.

units.zh: 微夫人之誠懇，大盜幾移國乎！
units.en: Without such hearts the usurper might have shifted the mandate!
units.literal: Without such men's earnest devotion—the great thief nearly stole the state!

units.zh: 道徽儒雅，柔而有正，協德始安，頗均連璧。
units.en: Xi Jian moved as the paired jades of his age—learned, supple, upright.
units.literal: Daohui cultured and gentle—yielding yet upright—joined virtue at restored peace—quite matching paired jades.

units.zh: 方回踵武，奕世登臺。
units.en: Xi Yin walked his father's path—generation after generation reached high office.
units.literal: Fanghui followed predecessor footprints—generations mounting terrace.

units.zh: 露冕為飾，援高人以同志，抑惟大隱者獻！
units.en: He wore office only as costume yet befriended hermits—a great recluse's paradox!
units.literal: Dew-bedecked crown as ornament—drawing lofty men as companions—is not this the offering of the great recluse!

units.zh: 愛子云亡，省遺文而輟泣，殊有大義之風矣。
units.en: When his brilliant son died Xi Yin burned his papers—then understood—and stopped worthless tears—there was noble principle there.
units.literal: Beloved son's cloud demise—reading leftover writings stopping tears—truly great righteousness's manner.

units.zh: 贊曰：太真懷貞，勤宣乃誠。
units.en: Verdict: Wen Jiao kept faith and proved it with deeds.
units.literal: The hymn says: Taizhen cherished fidelity—diligently proclaimed his sincerity.

units.zh: 謀敦翦峻，奮節摛名。
units.en: He broke Wang Dun and crushed Su Jun—his banner flew highest.
units.literal: He plotted against Wang Dun and struck Su Jun—raising integrity he seized fame.

units.zh: 道徽忠勁，高芬遠映。
units.en: Xi Jian stayed loyal—his scent travels far.
units.literal: Daohui loyal and stalwart—fragrant renown shines far.

units.zh: 愔克負荷，超慚雅正。
units.en: Xi Yin bore his father's mantle while Xi Chao, beside refinement, knew shame.
units.literal: Yin could bear the burden—Chao beside cultured correctness felt shame.
